Create Item: A wish can be used to create any item, mundane or magical. Instead of an active spell effect cost, you spend enough additional numen to bind the item (Chapter 6). If this causes you to exceed maximum, the item remains only so long as you are actively pursuing the current adventure. Inherent Bonuses to Attribute Scores: Attribute scores are not “shuffled,” as in the core rules. Rather, use of a wish to this end costs additional numen as appropriate to an inherent attribute score increase (Chapter 6). Again, this cost supersedes the active spell effect cost for the wish.

sections.heading: Metamagic
sections.text:
A great number of additional metamagic feats, beyond those in the core rules, are presented in here. This is done in hopes of making the “building blocks” of existing higher-level spells more transparent. As noted previously, most if not all published higher-level spells can ideally be treated simply as lower-level spells with appropriate metamagic feats added to them. Specific examples are provided below, and in the Grimoire (Appendix 8A).
Metamagic feats used in tandem, and the Heighten Spell feat in general, work somewhat differently than in 3.5/Pathfinder, as outlined below.

sections.heading: Metamagic Synergy
sections.text: Metamagic Synergy: If a spell is modified with a metamagic feat carrying a spell level cost of at least +1, each additional metamagic feat thereafter applied to that spell has its spell level cost, if positive, decreased by 1 (to a minimum of +1). This mechanism, in most cases, allows the final modified spell level to match that in the core rules. For example, a fireball spell is simply a 0-level jet of flame spell, with the Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) and Shape Spell (ray to burst: +3 -1 = +2) feats applied, for a final level of 0 + 1 + 2 = 3rd. Other examples are provided below, and in Appendix 8A.

sections.heading: Applying Metamagic
sections.text:
Metamagic can be applied normally: prepared casters must generally prepare the spells in advance in their modified form; spontaneous casters can apply metamagic spontaneously, which always requires a somatic component (but does not otherwise increase the casting time).
There are a few variations and additional options in these house rules, as described below.
Applying metamagic requires a Spellcraft check (Chapter 4) at a DC equal to 15 + the total spell level including metamagic costs (treating +0 costs as +1, and treating negative costs as if they were positive). This restriction does not apply to casting or preparing spells that come pre-modified (see below).
Metamagic Schools: Feats with a school descriptor cannot be used by specialists for whom that particular school is barred, even if the primary school is usable.
Pre-Modified Spells: Wizards and archivists might find pre-modified spells that can be scribed into their spellbooks at the appropriate (modified) spell level; this does not require the caster to know the metamagic feat in question. Likewise, a spontaneous caster might gain a spell pre-modified with metamagic directly as a spell known: for example, an incarnate could simply learn maximized searing light as a 5th level spell (with the normal casting time), rather than selecting searing light as a 3rd level spell and also taking the Maximize Spell feat. In this case, neither the unmodified spell nor the metamagic feat (for use on other spells) is available to the caster.
Innate Metamagic: Another option is to select the Innate Metamagic feat (q.v.) and apply it to a spell instead of a spell-like ability, allowing in essence a Sudden Metamagic feat (q.q.v.) usable only with that particular spell, but usable either 3/day (instead of 1/day), or at will with a sufficiently high number of ranks in Concentration. Although far superior to the above option in terms of spell level required, this option requires the expenditure of a feat.
Hero Points and Metamagic Feats: You can use hero points to spontaneously apply any metamagic feat you know without increasing the casting time and without increasing the spell level. For each level by which the spell level would normally be increased, this costs 1 hero point.
Mitigating Metamagic: Some metamagic feats have a negative cost—i.e., they reduce the final level of the modified spell. Negative-cost metamagic, when applied while preparing spells, requires an additional 1 hour per spell level worth of reduction (this does not apply to pre-modified spells). Metamagic feats that reduce the final spell level cannot be applied spontaneously.

sections.heading: Heightened Spells
sections.text: The effects of Heighten Spell are automatically applied whenever a spell’s level is increased by applying metamagic (e.g., a Maximized acid splash is treated as a 3rd level spell for all purposes, not as a 0-level spell). Heighten Spell can also be applied by itself; this requires a Spellcraft check (DC 20 + final level of the spell).

sections.heading: Effects of Heightening Spells
sections.text:
Many individual “seed” spells (see below) have automatic improvements when Heightened; these specified in the spell descriptions. Other more general examples are as follows.
Bonuses (Scaling): Spells providing scaling bonuses (e.g., “+1 per caster level”) have a bonus cap based on the final (modified) level of the spell. In general, 1st level spells provide a maximum bonus of +5 to one person. Higher-level spells can provide higher bonuses, according to the table below.
Spell Level | Single Target | Multiple Targets
1st | +5 | +0
2nd | +10 | +5
3rd | +10 | +10
4th | +15 | +10
5th | +15 | +15
6th | +20 | +15
7th | +20 | +20
8th | +25 | +20
9th | +25 | +25
Note that these are maxima. If a lower bonus cap is specified for the individual spell in question (e.g., skill enhancement—see below), then use that cap instead.
Direct-Damage Evocations: Most evocations deal 1d6 energy damage per caster level, with a maximum number of dice (“damage cap”) based on the final level of the spell (after adding metamagic feats).  Standard damage caps are modified from the 3.0 edition Dungeon Master’s Guide, as shown in the table below.
Spell Level | Arcane Spells: | Divine Spells:
Single Target | Multiple Targets | Single Target | Multiple Targets
0 | 1d6 | — | — | —
1 | 5d6 | 5d6 | 1d6 | —
2 | 10d6 | 5d6 | 5d6 | 5d6
3 | 10d6 | 10d6 | 10d6 | 5d6
4 | 15d6 | 10d6 | 10d6 | 10d6
5 | 15d6 | 15d6 | 15d6 | 10d6
6 | 20d6 | 15d6 | 15d6 | 15d6
7 | 20d6 | 20d6 | 20d6 | 15d6
8 | 25d6 | 20d6 | 20d6 | 20d6
9 | 25d6 | 25d6 | 25d6 | 20d6

sections.heading: Metamagic Feats
sections.text:
Unless otherwise noted, all [metamagic] feats in this section are also assumed to have the [arcane] descriptor, in addition to any others listed.
Prerequisites: In addition to the prerequisites listed, learning a metamagic feat requires a number of ranks in Spellcraft equal to 2 x the Metamagic Cost (see below).
Metamagic Cost: The “Metamagic Cost” entry is the increase in spell level that the feat applies to the base spell (e.g., a Metamagic Cost of “+1 level” means that the feat takes up a spell slot 1 level higher than the base spell). In many cases, this can be scaled in order to increase the effects.
“Missing” Feats: Most metamagic feats that directly inflicted a condition (e.g., Dazing Spell, Toppling Spell) are now simulated using Cascade Spell, with the appropriate condition seed spell (see below). The distinction is that spells should do something, whereas metamagic should modify spells.

sections.heading: Accursed Spell                                                  [Curse, Metamagic, Necromancy]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Hex Spell (q.v.).
Benefit: A spell modified by this feat becomes a [curse]. This has several effects:
The school of the spell changes to Necromancy. Any penalty it inflicts becomes a profane penalty (regardless of its original type). The saving throw (if applicable) changes to Intuition.The effects cannot be removed by dispel magic (remove curse, break enchantment, etc. are effective).
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.
Special: To make a curse permanent, you invest personal numen at the time of casting; pricing is as for a latent spell effect (see above), but applying the duration multiplier as for an active effect: spell level x caster level x 50 x duration multiplier. You can also state a deed which, if accomplished, ends the curse (the deed must be possible to be accomplished within 1 year, and help is permissible). If so, contingent pricing is used (Chapter 6), allowing you to ignore the duration multiplier.

sections.heading: Amplify Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Imbue Item.
Benefit: When placed into an item, an amplified spell functions at the activator’s caster level, rather than at the item’s. In addition, the save DC (if applicable) is calculated using the activator’s Charisma modifier. This feat has no effect on spells that are not imbued into items.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.
Source: Use this feat for staves, for example, pricing them at the minimum caster level to use the highest-level spell, after applying this feat to each spell. Such items will generally also use the Restricted Spell feat, requiring a particular casting type and level, for a -1 spell level adjustment that offsets the cost of this feat.

sections.heading: Augment Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: When you Augment a spell that has automatically scaling effects when Heightened, the spell is treated as if it were 1 level higher (if the effects scale by each spell level) or as if 1 “step” higher (if effects scale by a range of levels), for each level by which the spell is Augmented.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level per “step.” This cost is not factored in when determining the base bonus or effects that are then Augmented. When used to increase a spell’s damage cap, this cost is not reduced by metamagic synergy (see above). For example, a 4th level spell dealing 10d6 damage to multiple creatures, if Augmented to 5th level, has a final damage cap of 15d6 (10d6 for being 4th level, +1 step; not 20d6 (15d6 for being 5th level, +1 more step).
Order of Operations: As with Reduce Spell (q.v.), apply this feat after any other metamagic feats that modify the final spell level.
Synergy: When used in conjunction with metemagic feats that lower the final spell level, Augment Spell (to Heighten the effects) is applied after the cost reductions, not before. Therefore, it is not possible, for example, to construct a 0-level spell that has effects as if it were a 5th level spell. For player use, the only exception to this rule is the Restricted Spell feat (q.v.).
Special: Some “seed spells” (see below) can also have other, different improvements when Augmented (as listed for each); unless otherwise noted, those costs can be reduced by metamagic synergy.

sections.heading: Bane Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A spell that deals direct damage, when modified by this feat, deals additional damage to one or more types of creatures (examples from the core rules include water elementals and plant creatures; fungi, molds, slimes, oozes, and undead; etc.). Damage against the selected creatures is increased by one die type (e.g., 20d6 becomes 20d8 damage).
Metamagic Cost: +1 level. If the creature type is preselected for the spell when prepared or learned, and cannot be changed by the caster, then the adjustment is +0. You cannot add this feat to a spell more than once, nor can you apply this feat to a spell already modified by the Creature-Specific Spell feat (q.v.).
Special: This is similar to the Bane Magic feat in Chapter 5, but with a spell level adjustment because the creature type can be changed by the user.

sections.heading: Bouncing SpellAPG
sections.text:
[Metamagic, Transmutation]
You can direct a failed spell against a different target.
Benefit: Whenever a bouncing spell targeting a single creature has no effect on its intended target due to spell resistance or a successful saving throw, you may, as a swift action, redirect the full effect to another eligible target within range. The redirected spell behaves in all ways as if its new target were the original target for the spell.
Spells that affect a target in any way (including a lesser effect) on a successful saving throw may not be redirected in this manner, nor can touch spells or spells requiring an attack roll.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

sections.heading: Cascade SpellFOM,DMG1 [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: You can combine two spells into a single cascade spell. The range and area of effect (or target) of the cascade spells are equal to the lesser of those of the two spells. For cascaded spells with different durations, those durations can be tracked separately, or combined into a single duration equal to the lesser of the two. Casting time is equal to the longer of the two casting times. The cascaded spell requires all of the components listed for each of the constituent spells. In addition:
Damage caps and other Heightening effects (see above) are determined by final spell level, not for individual spells within a Cascade.When cascading spells of different schools, neither can be a barred school for the caster, or else the entire spell fails.
Once the two spells have been Cascaded, they are thereafter treated as a single spell, and can be modified as a unit using other metamagic feats (e.g., after being Cascaded together, two touch-range spells can be converted to a ray with a single application of the Reach Spell feat). An exception is if separate durations were maintained.
For purposes of specialist wizard, a cascade spell with one component in the specialist school is treated as a specialist school spell (but barred school restrictions for the other component spell(s) still apply).
Metamagic Cost: A cascade spell uses up a spell slot one level higher than the total level of both spells in the cascade. Adding a spell to an existing spell always results in at least a +1 spell level increase; you cannot start with a low-level spell, add negative level-cost metamagic, and then Cascade that onto an existing spell with the net effect of lowering the other spell’s level. There are other specific rules when using Reduce Spell (q.v.) in conjunction with this feat.
Synergy: It is not possible to Cascade multiple damage-inflicting spells together in order to inflict total damage greater than the (final) level-based damage caps shown under Effects of Heightening Spells, above. To deal multiple types of damage, the Energy Admixture feat (see above) is used instead.
Special: In some of the example spells from the Grimoire, a Cascaded spell that adversely affects the caster is included, with a negative metamagic cost equal to the level of the Cascaded spell (this applies only if the Cascaded spell is appropriately dangerous or harmful to the caster, per the referee’s discretion). This simulates the “corruption cost” of Corrupt spellsBVD,HH.

sections.heading: Channel Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A channeled spell can be discharged through a weapon attack. This otherwise works as a touch spell (in terms of casting and Holding the Charge); the only difference is in the delivery. The next time you strike an opponent with that weapon, the spell discharges. The target takes the normal damage and effects of a successful attack in addition to the spell's effect.
You can place a channeled spell on a piece of ammunition or a projectile, such as a sling bullet, an arrow, or a crossbow bolt. In such a case, the spell dissipates if the attack misses. The spell cannot be placed on a bow, crossbow, sling, or similar weapon that uses ammunition.
If the weapon is an eldritch blast (or other similar attack ability), only the creature struck is affected, even if the spell normally affects multiple targets or an area. Only if the eldritch blast itself is modified to affect an area (as with the Shape Spell feat) or multiple targets (as with the Ray Splitting feat) can a channeled spell affecting an area or multiple targets do so. Likewise, if the spell normally affects only a single target, but the eldritch blast or other ability affects multiple targets or an area, then the spell applies to only one of the targets within the area of effect.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level. You cannot use the Manifested Spell feat (q.v.) in order to defray this cost.
Synergy:
In order to Channel a spell into multiple attacks, also apply the Ray Splitting feat (q.v.).If you Extend (q.v.) an instantaneous Channeled spell, the weapon used to channel the spell can be used throughout that time period—i.e., it becomes, in essence, a temporary magic item.
Special: In some cases, this feat can be used to channel a spell through some object or manifestation other than a weapon—Cf. project image in Appendix 8A.
Source: Smiting SpellPHII. This feat also supersedes the Eldritch Theurge’s spellblast and greatreach blast prestige class featuresCM.
Coaxing SpellPC [Metamagic]
Prerequisite: Profession (mining) 1 rank or favored terrain: underground (for oozes); or Survival 1 rank (for plants and vermin).
Benefit: This feat works only on [mind-affecting] spells, and spells inflicting other effects to which oozes, plants, and/or vermin are normally immune. A coaxing spell affects those creature types despite their normal immunity, but other creature types are immune. Cf. Threnodic Spell (q.v.).
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels. If you increase the cost to +2 levels (essentially removing the implied “Creature-Specific Spell” metamagic of this feat), the spell affects other targets normally.
Normal: Oozes, plants, and vermin are immune to [mind-affecting] spells and effects, and to attribute penalties, damage, and drain.

sections.heading: Communal SpellUC [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: The effects of a communal spell can be applied to any willing creatures. However, the total duration is divided as evenly as possible among the recipients you select, in increments equal to the duration’s time units (rounds, minutes, hours, etc.). Any unused duration is wasted.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Concentration Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
With concentration, you can maintain spells beyond their normal durations.
Prerequisite: Extend Spell.
Benefit: The duration of a Concentration Spell is equal to the length of time you concentrate, plus the spell’s normal duration thereafter. Concentrating to maintain a spell generally requires a standard action, and you must succeed at a Concentration check (DC 10 + twice the level of the spell) to maintain concentration on it. Anything that could break your concentration when casting a spell (e.g., you are threatened and fail to cast defensively, or take damage) can also break your concentration while you're maintaining one, causing the spell to end.
For spells that would normally have an instantaneous duration, you can redirect the effect once per round, for as long as you concentrate. For area-effect spells, you can move the effect up to 30 ft. per round. Any portion of the area that would extend beyond your maximum range dissipates harmlessly, reducing the remaining area thereafter. Because the effect is re-directed from round to round, it does not count as continuing damage for purposes of forcing Concentration checks (Chapter 4) from those affected.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels. By increasing the cost, you can maintain a Concentration spell more efficiently:
Partial action: +3 levels;Swift action: +4 levels.

sections.heading: Consecrate SpellCD                                                 [Divine, Good, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Any [good] alignment.
Benefit: This feat adds the [good] descriptor to a spell and may have an additional effect:
If the spell deals damage, half of the damage (rounded down) is holy damage resulting directly from divine power, and is therefore not subject to be reduced by resistance or immunity to energy-based attacks. If the spell provides a numerical bonus, the bonus type changes to [sacred].
Note that arcane spells generally cannot be modified with this feat.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Corrupt SpellCD [Divine, Evil, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Any [evil] alignment.
Benefit: This feat adds the [evil] descriptor to a spell. If the spell deals damage, half of the damage (rounded down) is unholy damage resulting directly from divine power, and is therefore not subject to be reduced by resistance or immunity to energy-based attacks. If the spell provides a numerical bonus, the bonus type changes to [profane].
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Creature-Specific Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Game designer (only)—not for PCs.
Benefit: A creature-specific spell affects only one creature type; others are immune. Examples include humanoids, plants, animals, aberrations and chaotic evil outsiders, creatures with the [aquatic] or [water] subtype, etc. Spells that already affect specific creature types (e.g., hold person) already have this feat incorporated into them; it cannot be applied again.
Metamagic Cost: -2 levels. If the spell can affect two creature types, rather than only one, the cost is -1 level instead.
Special: This “feat” is included here in order to show the theoretical construction of such spells as daze person. It is not intended for general use as a standard feat.
As shown below and in Appendix 8A, variants are also possible—e.g., an “Item-Specific Spell” for spells that can only be cast on specific items (e.g., pyrotechnics, on a bonfire), or a “Location-Specific Spell” for something like a spider climb that only works on one particular wall, for example.

sections.heading: Cross-Class Spell [Transmutation]
sections.text:
Benefit: A cross-class spell is treated as if it is on some other class spell list, chosen when the spell is learned or prepared. For example, cure light wounds might be made into an arcane spell using this feat.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level (if applied to a spell with the Restricted Spell feat, the cost is either +1 or +2 levels, as needed to offset the level reduction from that feat).

sections.heading: Delay SpellCA [Metamagic, Transmutation]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Extend Spell.
Benefit: When casting a Delayed spell, you set a delay before it takes effect. This can take one of three forms:
Time Lapse: You set a specific delay at the time of casting (the delay time cannot be changed once set; the spell activates just before your turn on the round you designate). Activating Condition: You can specify an activating condition outside of your control, such as “read by any creature” (if cast as a glyph or symbol) or “approached within 30 ft.”Trigger: You set a trigger, such as a command word, or need to throw a material component, etc., enabling you to trigger the spell at any time as a standard, move, or even swift action (at greater metamagic cost).
Only area and touch spells can be affected by this feat. Any decisions you would make about the spell (including attack rolls, designating targets, or determining or shaping an area) are decided when the spell is cast. Any of its effects outside of your control (including damage and saving throws) determined when the spell triggers.
If conditions change during the delay period in ways that would make the spell impossible to cast (the target you designate moves beyond the spell's range, for example), the spell fails. During the delay period, a delayed spell can be dispelled normally, and it can be detected in the area or on the target (as applicable).
If you delay a spell for more than 1 hour/level, you must invest personal numen to maintain the latent spell effect (see Latent Spells, above).
Metamagic Cost: By activation:
Activation | Metamagic Cost
Time lapse or activating condition | +2 levels
Trigger (standard action) | +2 levels
Trigger (partial action) | +3 levels
Trigger (swift action) | +4 levels
In addition to the metamagic cost, latent spells carry a numen cost to maintain (see above).

sections.heading: Disguise SpellSRD [Illusion, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Bluff and Sleight of Hand (or Perform, if applicable to disguise used) 6 ranks; or Bardic inspiration and Perform (music) or Linguistics 6 ranks.
Benefit: You have mastered the art of casting spells unobtrusively, mingling verbal and somatic components into rhythm and performance (or some other activity) so that others rarely catch you in the act of casting a spell. Like a silent, stilled spell, a disguised spell can’t be identified through Spellcraft. An observer must succeed at a Perception check (opposed by a Bluff or Sleight of Hand check on your part) to even be aware that you are initiating some sort of magical effect; your performance or recitation is obvious to everyone in the vicinity, but the fact that you are casting a spell isn’t. Unless the spell visibly emanates from you or observers have some other means of determining its source, they don’t know where the effect came from.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Drain, Crippling
sections.text:
[Metamagic, Necromancy]
Benefit: Attribute damage dealt by a crippling drain spell becomes attribute drain instead; a temporary negative level is similarly converted to a potentially permanent one (Cf. damage attribute, enervation).
Metamagic Cost: For every 1d4 of attribute damage converted to attribute drain, or for each temporary negative level to be made potentially permanent, a Crippling Drain spell uses up a spell slot one level higher than the spell's actual level.

sections.heading: Empathic Spell [Enchantment, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can only be applied to a spell that grants a numerical bonus of some type (enhancement, insight, sacred, etc.). The bonus type changes to Morale, and the spell gains the [mind-affecting] descriptor.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Empower Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can increase the power of your spells, causing them to deal more damage.
Benefit: All variable, numeric effects of an empowered spell are increased by one-half, so an Empowered fireball from a 10th level caster deals 1.5 x 10d6 damage. Range, duration, and other level- dependent parameters are not increased, but level-based bonuses and effects expressed in numbers of dice are. For example, an Empowered cure light wounds from a 5th level caster heals (1d6+5) x 1.5 damage, not (1d6 x 1.5) + 5. Spells without numerically-driven effects are not affected.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels. These levels do not themselves count towards Heightening the base spell.
Synergy: If a Maximized spell (q.v.) is also Empowered, apply the effects separately, as if neither feat were initially present. For example, an Empowered, Maximized 10-die fireball deals (0.5 x 10d6) + 60 damage, not 90.

sections.heading: Special
sections.text: Special: This feat is a specific case of the Cascade Spell feat (q.v.): Transmute (1st level) + Augment Spell (rare metal; +2 levels) + Effect-Specific Spell (direct-damage evocation; -1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to inst.; -1 level) = 1st level.

sections.heading: Evocation, Adamantine                           [Evocation, Metamagic, Transmutation]
sections.text:
Benefit: Bludgeoning, piercing, and/or slashing damage inflicted by an Adamantine spell bypass up to 20 points of damage reduction or hardness, as if by an adamantine weapon.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

sections.heading: Evocation, Conductive                              [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This metamagic feat can be applied only to spells that have the [cold], [fire], [electricity], or [sonic] descriptor. Against metal-armored creatures, creatures holding metal weapons/objects, or creatures that are actually made of metal (such as iron golems), conductive spells gain a +4 circumstance bonus to attack rolls (for spells requiring attack rolls) and/or a +4 circumstance bonus to the save DC (for those allowing a saving throw).
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Evocation, Energy Admixture                [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
You have learned to marry the power of two different energy types.
Prerequisite: Spellcraft 1 rank (see table below).
Benefit: When you cast a spell that deals energy damage, you can cause half of the damage inflicted to correspond to a different energy type, according to the table below. The spell’s descriptor changes to include both energy types or descriptors.
Metamagic Cost: As shown in the table below.
Damage Type | Ranks in Spellcraft | Metamagic Cost
Acid, cold, electricity, fire | 1 | +0
Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing | 6 | +0
Sonic, negative energy | 11 | +1
Force | 16 | +2
Source: This feat supersedes Born of Three ThundersCA and Lord of the UttercoldCA feats, and also the Daggerspell Mage’sCAd invocation of the knife prestige class feature.

sections.heading: Evocation, Inexorable                                   [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can be applied only to spells that deal hit point damage. An inexorable evocation spell does not allow a saving throw for half damage.
Metamagic Cost: +4 levels.
Special: In some cases, existing spells other than evocations (e.g., irresistible dance) are “built” using this feat. These are special cases and should not be taken as license for player use in that manner, unless the referee and other players are all in agreement.

sections.heading: Evocation, Lingering                                 [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This metamagic feat can be applied only to a spell that has an energy descriptor (e.g., [acid] or [fire]). Creatures and objects damaged by a lingering evocation spell must succeed at Reflex saves (DC equal to the spell DC) or take an additional 1d6 damage each round (of the same energy type) until the save is made, the damage is negated (by dousing the flames for lingering fire damage, rinsing with water for acid damage, etc.), or for a maximum of 1 round per rank in Concentration you possess.
The continuing damage from Lingering Evocation forces those affected to succeed at Concentration checks (Chapter 4) to use spells or spell-like abilities.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level. You can increase the lingering damage by using progressively higher-level spell slots: +2 levels for 2d6/round; +3 levels for 1d6 +1d6 per 2 levels of the final spell level, rounded up (e.g., a Lingering fireball, cast as a 5th level spell, would deal 4d6 burn damage per round), minimum 3d6.
Source: This feat allows the construction of a number of spells from the Core rules. Used with the Innate Metamagic feat and applied to a sorcerer’s eldritch blast, this feat stands in for the Warlock’sCA brimstone blast and vitriolic blast invocations. Applied to a fire-based eldritch blast and channeled into unarmed attacks, it also subsumes the Efreeti StanceUC feat.

sections.heading: Special
sections.text: Special: This feat is a specific case of the Cascade Spell feat (q.v.): Warding (energy resistance; 1st level) + Irresistible Spell (+3 levels) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to inst.; -2 levels) + Restricted Spell (evoker, or bloodline, domain, etc. with appropriate energy descriptor; -1 level) = 1st level.

sections.heading: [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your spells of a specific energy type can damage creatures and objects that normally have resistance or immunity.
Prerequisites: Evoker or access to bloodline, domain, mystery, etc. with appropriate energy descriptor.
Benefit: Upon selecting this feat, choose one energy type for which you meet the prerequisites (the feat also gains that energy descriptor).
Spells dealing that type of energy damage, when modified by this feat, deal full damage to creatures with resistance to that energy type, and deal full damage to objects that are not otherwise immune to that energy type (bypassing hardness, etc.). Against creatures or objects normally immune to that energy type, the energy damage is reduced by half.
Creatures and objects affected by an Overwhelming spell are still entitled to whatever saving throw the spell normally allows, and to SR if applicable.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.
Source: This feat supersedes the Piercing Cold EvocationFB and Searing EvocationSSt feats.

sections.heading: Evocation, Splash [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can be applied only to spells that require attack rolls. A Splash evocation deals 1 point of damage per final level of the spell (minimum 1) of the appropriate type to all targets adjacent to the creature, object, or square hit by the spell (in the event of a miss, treat a ranged spell as a grenade-like missile to determine the square hit).
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.
Source: This feat allows construction of alchemist’s fire and acid flasks; see Appendix 6A.

sections.heading: Evocation, Versatile                                   [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can alter the damage type of the spell in question.
Benefit: Choose a damage type from the list below. When you prepare or spontaneously cast a damage-dealing spell, you can apply this feat in order to change the damage type from the original type to the type you selected.
Metamagic Cost: +0 for acid, bludgeoning, cold, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing; +1 for sonic or negative energy; +2 for force.
Synergy: In conjunction with the Cross-Class Spell feat to provide the [water] descriptor, this supersedes the Benthic SpellPC feat.
Special: An evoker (Chapter 3) has a superior version of this feat as a class feature.

sections.heading: Expedient Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
An expedient spell is designed to deal with weaker opponents, allowing a caster to save higher-level spell slots for more formidable threats.
Benefit: An expedient spell can affect only a limited number of Hit Dice. Choose one of the following options:
Total HD Affected: The spell affects a total number of HD worth of creatures. Creatures with the fewest HD are affected first, and among creatures with equal HD, those who are closest to the spell's point of origin are affected first. HD that are not sufficient to affect a creature are wasted. This option cannot be applied to a spell that normally affects only a single target.
Final Spell Level | Total HD Affected
1st | 2d4
2nd – 3rd | 2d4 + 1/level (+5 max.)
4th – 5th | 2d4 + 1/level (+10 max.)
6th – 7th | 2d4 + 1/level (+15 max.)
8th – 9th | 2d4 + 1/level (+20 max.)
Individual HD Affected: The maximum HD of each creature to be affected is equal to 4 + the final level of the spell. Creatures with higher HD than this limit are immune.
Individual hp Affected: The spell has full effect only targets whose current hit point total is less than or equal to 11x the level of the spell. For limited-duration effects, creatures with up to 22x the level of the spell are also affected, but the duration is reduced by 1 time step (e.g., minutes to rounds).
Metamagic Cost: -1 level.

sections.heading: Explosive SpellCA [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can cast spells that blast creatures back out of the area.
Benefit: On a failed Reflex save, an explosive spell ejects any creature caught its area, sending it to a location outside the nearest edge of that area and dealing additional damage. For example, all creatures in the area of an explosive fireball that fail their saving throws not only take full damage but are pushed to the closest square outside the perimeter of the spell's 20-foot-radius spread. Likewise, an explosive lightning bolt moves targets that fail their saves to outside the area defined by the squares the bolt's line passes through (any creature struck dead-on, determined by a ranged touch attack, is pushed the full length of the line).
Any creature moved in this manner also takes an additional 1d6 points of bludgeoning damage per 10 feet moved (no additional damage if moved less than 10 feet by the effect; maximum 10d6 if moved 100 ft. or more). If some obstacle prevents a blasted creature from being moved to the edge of the effect, the creature is stopped and takes 1d6 damage from striking the barrier (in addition to any damage taken from the distance moved before then). In any event, this movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Explosive Spell can be applied only to spells that allow Reflex saves and affect an area.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

sections.heading: Extend Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can make your spells last longer than normal.
Benefit: An Extended spell lasts longer than normal.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level to double the duration. The pricing for other changes in duration is as follows:
Original Duration | New Duration:
1 rd. or | 1 rd. | 1 min. | 10 min. | 1 hr. | 2 hrs.
Inst. | /level
Instant. | +2 | +3 | +4 | +5 | +6 | +7
1 round | — | +2 | +3 | +4 | +5 | +6
1 rd./lvl | -1 | — | +2 | +3 | +4 | +5
1 min./lvl | -2 | -1 | — | +2 | +3 | +4
10 min./lvl | -3 | -2 | -1 | — | +2 | +3
1 hr./lvl | -4 | -3 | -2 | -1 | — | +2
For seed spells with a duration of “Concentration,” treat the duration as being 1 round for purposes of this feat.
Special: When a direct-damage spell with an instantaneous duration is Extended, its effects apply each round individually. For area-effect spells, that means the damage onset is instantaneous, but applies to all within the area. For targeted spells, the damage re-occurs round by round; because the effect is re-applied each round individually, it does not count as continuing damage for purposes of forcing Concentration checks from those affected.
Note that spells can be made to last more than 2 hours per level by investing personal numen in them as if they were magic items; see “Active Spells,” above.

sections.heading: Fell Condition [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: Select one condition or condition type (e.g., blindness, or [affliction] or [fear]; see Chapter 7). When you cast a spell with that imposes a minor condition with that descriptor for multiple rounds, even targets that successfully save are affected for 1 round.
If the spell normally imposes a more severe condition on a failed saving throw, a successful save imposes the associated minor condition instead, for the same length of time that the more severe condition would otherwise last.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.
Special: Because this is actually a set of feats, different names can be used depending on the condition chosen—e.g., Fell Binding, Fell Dazzling, Fell Fatigue, Fell Frightening, Fell Sickening, Fell Staggering, etc.
Source: Based on the Fell FrighteningLM feat.

sections.heading: Hex Spell [Curse, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: When applied to a spell that normally provides a numerical bonus (e.g., attribute boost, enhancement, etc.), a Hex spell confers an equivalent numerical penalty instead. This feat cannot be used to turn penalties into bonuses.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.
Special: In some cases, it may be possible to apply this feat to spells that have other effects; e.g., a Hex bestow feat spell might make the target lose the specified feat instead of gaining it; a Hex alter senses might remove a sense rather than granting or augmenting it. Referee discretion is required for these uses.

sections.heading: Special
sections.text: Special: This feat is a specific case of the Cascade Spell feat (q.v.): Glamer (1st level) + Augment Spell (invisibility; +2 levels) + Effect-Specific Spell (spell Cascaded to; -2 levels) = 1st level.

sections.heading: Hide SpellRR                                                 [Evocation, Illusion Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A Hidden spell has no visual or auditory manifestation. Those targeted or within the area of effect are considered flat-footed to the effects of the spell, and lose their Dex bonus to Reflex saves against it, unless they possess the Alertness feat (Chapter 5) and at least 4 ranks in Perception.
Metamagic Cost: +2 spell levels. For each time increment step greater than 1 rd./level the base spell lasts (q.v., Extend Spell), increase the metamagic cost by +1 level.

sections.heading: Innate Metamagic [Skill]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Able to use spell-like abilities or to cast spells; Concentration 2+ ranks (see below).
Benefit: Choose one spell-like ability you possess or one spell known. You can apply any one metamagic feat of your choice to that spell or spell-like ability, without increasing the casting time or the actual level of the spell. You need not know the metamagic feat in question. Once the spell-like ability (or spell) and metamagic feat are selected, they cannot be changed.
You must meet a minimum number of ranks in Concentration to be able to apply this feat to any given spell or spell-like ability, depending on what the final (modified) level of the spell would be (spell level + normal metamagic cost). If you exceed the minimum number of ranks by a certain ratio, you can apply the metamagic effect spontaneously additional times per day, per the following table:
Final Spell Level | Minimum Skill Ranks for X uses/day:
1/day | 3/day | At will
1st | 1 | 3 | 5
2nd | 3 | 6 | 9
3rd | 5 | 9 | 13
4th | 7 | 12 | 17
5th | 9 | 15 | ―
6th | 11 | 18 | ―
7th | 13 | ― | ―
8th | 15 | ― | ―
9th | 17 | ― | ―
For example, a spell-like ability of scorching ray (a 2nd level spell) could be Empowered (normally +2 levels cost, for a final level of 4th) once per day by a caster with at least 7 ranks in Concentration, three times per day by a caster with at least 12 ranks in Concentration, and at will by a caster with at least 17 ranks.
Spell-like abilities gained as class features that do not have a designated spell level are treated as if they were of a level equal to half the class level at which they are obtained (round up). For example, the various 1st level clerical domain spell-like abilities count as 1st level spells, for purposes of this feat.
Special: You can gain this feat multiple times; each time, it applies to a different spell or spell-like ability and/or metamagic feat. In the case of multiple Innate Metamagics applied to a single spell or spell-like ability, calculate the minimum Concentration ranks using the total metamagic cost (see Metamagic Feats introduction).
Source: This feat supersedes the various spell-like ability metamagic feats (Empower Spell-Like Ability, Quicken Spell-Like Ability, etc.), and also provides a metamagic option not available to sorcerers, bards, incarnates, etc. in the CRB. When applied to a sorcerer’s eldritch blast, it supersedes the Warlock’sCA various blast invocations. When applied to a spell known, it supersedes the Wu Jen’sCA spell secret and the Theologian’sUM domain secret class features.
This feat can be applied in reverse to remove the [language-dependent] metamagic feat from spells that have it (+1 level metamagic cost for this use); this supersedes the Tattood Mystic’s twisting script prestige class featurePoP.

sections.heading: Interrupting Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Quicken Spell or Sudden Spell.
Benefit: There are two ways in which this feat can be applied:
A spell with a casting time of 1 swift action gains a new casting time of 1 immediate action, allowing you can cast the spell even when it’s not your turn.Alternatively, you can apply this feat to a spell that is Delayed until some pre-determined event (see Delay Spell, q.v.); when activated, that spell can interrupt the event that triggered it.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Insightful Spell [Divination, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can only be applied to a spell that grants a numerical bonus of some type (enhancement, morale, sacred, etc.). The bonus type changes to insight, and the school of the spell changes to Divination.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

sections.heading: Irresistible Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: An irresistible spell does not allow spell resistance. Alternatively, this feat can be applied to a divination or teleportation spell to allow the effect to pass through stone walls, etc. (see “Castles and Dungeons,” above).
Metamagic Cost: +3 levels.

sections.heading: Language-Dependent Spell   [Enchantment, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A language-dependent spell uses intelligible language as a medium for communication. If a target cannot understand or hear what the caster of a language-dependent spell says, the spell has no effect on that creature, even if the target fails its saving throw. A spell with this feat applied to it gains the [language-dependent] descriptor.
Cost: -1 level.

sections.heading: Lucky Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Bard, halfling, or access to Chaos or Fate domain.
Benefit: This feat can only be applied to a spell that grants a numerical bonus of some type (enhancement, morale, sacred, etc.). The bonus type changes to Luck.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

sections.heading: Manifested Spell [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your damaging spells appear as weapons, and can be defended against with armor and shield.
Benefit: This feat can be applied only to spells that require a touch attack or ranged touch attack roll. A manifested spell strikes against the target’s normal AC, rather than touch AC. For spells that require a normal melee attack roll, the manifested spell may add the wielder’s Strength modifier to damage (evaluate on a case-by-case basis, as appropriate for the spell).
Metamagic Cost: -1 level.
Source: This feat is used in the construction of spell-created weapons such as spiritual weapon and Mordenkainen’s sword.

sections.heading: Special
sections.text: Special: For touch range spells, a similar effect can be simulated using Shape Spell (ray to burst; +3 levels) + Selective Spell (+1 level), for a final metamagic cost of +4 levels.

sections.heading: Mass Effect Spell                                          [Metamagic, Transmutation]
sections.text:
Your spells can affect more targets.
Benefit: A spell that normally affects a single target (e.g., hold person) can be modified to affect more than one target within range.
Instead of affecting multiple targets, this feat can be applied to modify a spell to affect multiple parameters (e.g., multiple attributes, with the attribute boost spell seed). You cannot use this feat in conjunction with the acid splash seed (see below) to deal multiple types of stacking energy damage exceeding the damage cap for that spell’s level (see Effects of Heightening Spells, above). Instead, the Energy Admixture feat (q.v.) is used.
Metamagic Cost: By number of targets:
Number of Targets | Metamagic Cost
2 | +2 levels
1/3 levels (min. 1) | +3 levels
1/level | +4 levels
Source: Suggested by the various “mass X” spellsCRB. This feat also subsumes the Chain SpellCA,RR feat. Combined with the Innate Metamagic feat, this supersedes the Warlock’sCA eldritch chain invocation.

sections.heading: Maximize Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your spells have the maximum possible effect.
Benefit: All variable, numeric effects of a spell modified by this feat are maximized. Saving throws and opposed rolls are not affected, nor are spells without random variables.
Metamagic Cost: +3 levels.
Synergy: An empowered (q.v.), maximized spell gains the separate benefits of each feat: the maximum result plus one-half the normally rolled result.

sections.heading: Merciful SpellAPG [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your damaging spells subdue rather than kill.
Benefit: You can alter spells that inflict damage to inflict nonlethal (subdual) damage instead. Spells that inflict damage of a particular type (such as fire) inflict nonlethal damage of that same type.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.

sections.heading: Metamagic Spell TriggerCM
sections.text:
You can apply metamagic feats you know to spell trigger magic items you activate.
Prerequisites: Any metamagic feat, Spellcraft 12 ranks.
Benefit: You can apply any one metamagic feat you know to a spell generated by a spell trigger item (such as a wand or staff) that you activate. You expend one extra charge for each change in spell level a metamagic feat normally requires. If the metamagic feat's level adjustment would normally increase the slot of the chosen spell's level above the maximum spell level you can normally cast, you can't apply the metamagic effect to the spell. For example, a caster with access to 9th level spells cannot apply Quicken Spell to an antimagic field generated by a staff (since that would take a 10th level spell slot to cast).
If sufficient charges aren't available in the item to power the application of metamagic feats (or if the item doesn't use charges), the item fails to activate and no charges are used, but the action used to activate the item is wasted.
Special: If the item is usable at will (i.e., has unlimited charges), this feat cannot be used with that item.

sections.heading: Natural Spell [Metamagic, Transmutation]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Wis 13, ability to assume non-speaking form.
Benefit: A Natural Spell’s verbal and somatic components are modified to suit a particular non-humanoid form and voice, such as a bird or fish. You can also use any material components or focuses you possess in that form, even if such items are melded into that form.
You can therefore prepare Natural spells that you can cast while using wild shape, polymorph, or the like. You cannot cast spells modified with this feat while in your normal form, or in a form with different limbs than the one it was intended for (e.g., you cannot cast a Natural Spell for frogs while in the form of a bird).
This feat does not permit the use of magic items while you are in a form that could not ordinarily use them, and you do not gain the ability to speak while shapeshifted.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.
Synergy: If you also have the Variable Spell feat, you can apply that as well (at its normal metamagic cost), allowing a Natural Spell to be cast in any form you take.

sections.heading: Pacific Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Pacific spells have only limited utility in combat.
Benefit: When this spell is applied to a beneficial spell (“buff”), the spell’s effects end immediately if the affected creature makes an attack (including use of offensive spells).
An offensive spell modified with this metamagic, if used in combat, provides each target with a +2 circumstance bonus on its saving throw (if applicable), or has a 50% chance of failing outright (if not). For offensive spells with ongoing durations, any hostile or violent act towards a target allows a second saving throw or check to end the effects. The same is true if the spell leads the target(s) into a dangerous area.
Spells with no direct offensive or defensive uses (e.g., dancing lights) cannot be modified using this feat.
Metamagic Cost: -2 levels.

sections.heading: Pattern Spell [Illusion, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can be applied only to spells with durations greater than Instantaneous. A Pattern spell relies on a visual display in order to function. Any creature unable to see the display is unaffected; this applies to blinded creatures, those without a line of sight, those intentionally closing their eyes at the time of casting, etc. Any breaking of the line of sight during the duration ends the effect on that creature immediately. The school of a Pattern spell changes to Illusion [pattern].
Metamagic Cost: -1 level.
Special: This feat can be modified to require an auditory or olfactory effect instead. Once the required sense is selected, it cannot be changed.
Synergy: For gaze attacks, modify a spell to an emanation using the Shape Spell feat (q.v.), and add this feat to simulate the visual contact needed.

sections.heading: Penetrating Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your spells bypass spell resistance more easily.
Benefit: When casting a Penetrating spell, you gain a +2 enhancement bonus to Concentration checks to overcome the target’s spell resistance.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level. You can increase this cost as desired; each additional spell level increases the bonus by +2.

sections.heading: Permanent Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
One of your spells is constantly active, without the need to prepare or cast it.
Prerequisites: Concentration 8 ranks + 1 rank per level of the spell, Extend Spell feat.
Benefit: Cast one spell you know with duration of 1 hour per level (if normally shorter, you must apply Extend Spell first). The effects of that single casting of the spell become permanent. If successfully dispelled, the permanent spell is merely suppressed for 2d4 rounds. You can use this feat in three ways:
On yourself. This can be any spell with a range of personal, or any spell that targets you specifically or has a mobile emanation centered on you (it cannot be used on spells that are discharged). For permanent spells such as detect magic or detect thoughts, you need not concentrate to be aware of the mere presence of absence of the things detected, but you must still concentrate to gain additional information, as normal. Concentration on such a spell is a standard action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity.On another willing creature. In that case, the recipient of the spell selects this feat (and need not meet the prerequisites), but you cast the spell. For example, a cleric could imbue a fighter companion with a permanent +3 sacred bonus to attacks and damage (by means of an Extended divine favor spell); the fighter would have to select Permanent Spell as a feat in order to gain this effect. The recipient must also have a minimum HD equal to 8 + the level of the spell to be made permanent, or the effect fails.For permanent spells that affect an object, area, or unwilling creature, you instead invest personal numen, as described above and in Chapter 6; this feat is not used.
Special: You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, it applies to a different casting of a different spell.
Source: This feat supersedes the permanency spell from the core rules and subsumes the Permanent Emanation featSRD. It is also proposed as a means to allow somewhat the same effect as the Persistent Spell featCA, without that feat’s seemingly limitless potential for abuse.

sections.heading: Personal Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A personal spell can only be cast on yourself. The range becomes “personal,” and the target is “you.”
Special: Spells that already have those parameters are assumed to have been constructed using this feat, and it therefore cannot be applied again.
Metamagic Cost: -1 level.
Special: This feat is included as a consequence of “reverse-engineering” some of the existing 3.5/Pathfinder spells. However, its use runs directly contrary to the design goal of encouraging team play. For that reason, many groups will choose not to include it as an option.

sections.heading: Phantasmal Spell                                               [Illusion, Metamagic, Mind-Affecting]shafts
sections.text:
“Let us hope that our theory is correct, and that their shafts are powerless against minds cognizant of their unreality.”
--Edgar Rice Burroughs, Thuvia, Maid of Mars (1916)
Prerequisite: Spell Focus (Illusion) or illusionist wizard specialist.
Benefit: This feat is most commonly applied to non-illusions, but can also be applied to illusions. The effects depend on the type of spell it is applied to.
Illusions: If applied to an Illusion spell (Cf. figment and glamer seeds, below), the illusion is only in the mind of one creature to be affected, rather than being perceptible to all those nearby. Its subschool descriptor changes from [figment] or [glamer] to [phantasm], and it also gains the [mind-affecting] descriptor. In order to affect more than one creature, the Mass Effect Spell or Shape Spell feat must be applied.
Non-Illusions: The effects of the Phantasmal spell are not real; the spell’s school changes to Illusion [mind-affecting, phantasm]. All those potentially affected receive an Intuition save to avoid all effects entirely. If this save is failed, the target(s) are subject to the original spell (and can roll an additional, normal saving throw against that spell, if applicable), and also suffer 3d6 nonlethal damage.
Metamagic Cost: -1 level.

sections.heading: Poison SpellDU [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can mystically transfer a poison to the target of your spells.
Prerequisite: Craft (Toxicology) 2 ranks per final spell level of the spell to be affected.
Benefit: You can add a contact or injury poison as a material component to a melee touch spell you are casting. Doing this entails the same risk of poisoning yourself as applying poison to a weapon.The target of the spell, in addition to being subject to the normal effects of the spell, is also exposed to the poison (the spell must deal damage to deliver the effect of an injury poison).
The dose of poison used as the component is expended when you cast the spell, whether or not the spell or poison successfully affects the target.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.

sections.heading: Positive SpellLM [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your spells channel positive energy to deal extra damage to undead creatures, but are less effective against other opponents.
Prerequisite: Ability to channel positive energy.
Benefit: This feat can only be applied to spells that deal hit point damage. A positive spell is infused with positive energy; it deals an extra 50% damage to undead creatures, but deals 50% less damage to non-undead creatures and to objects.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.
Synergy: If applied to a damaging spell with the [light] descriptor, the spell also damages molds, fungi, oozes, and slimes as if they were undead. If the spell generates at least bright light, undead specifically harmed by bright light or sunlight are also destroyed by the spell on a failed save.
You cannot apply this feat in conjunction with the Creature-Specific Spell or Bane Spell feat.

sections.heading: Psionic Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Eschew Materials.
Benefit: A psionic spell relies on mental (psionic) energy, rather than standard magic. It penetrates spell resistance, works in an antimagic field or globe of invulnerability, cannot be dispelled using dispel magic, etc. (unless the latter also have this feat as a component). However, it is susceptible to power resistance, an antipsionic field, dispel psionics, etc.
A spell modified with this feat has full effectiveness against other spells that incorporate this feat.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.
Normal: Magic-psionics transparency is a baseline assumption: i.e., psionic powers are affected by spell resistance, dispel magic, and so on, and spells are affected by power resistance, anipsionic field, etc.

sections.heading: Special
sections.text: Special: This is essentially a compound metamagic feat: Selective Spell (good; +3 levels) + Bane Spell (evil; +0 levels) + Restricted Spell (good caster; -1 level) = +2 levels.

sections.heading: Purify SpellBED [Good, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: [Good] descriptor
Benefits: A hit point damage-dealing spell modified using these feat does no damage to [good] creatures; against [evil] creatures, damage d6s are increased to d8s.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

sections.heading: Quicken Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can cast spells in a fraction of the normal time.
Prerequisites: Silent Spell, Still Spell.
Benefit: A Quickened spell can be directed as a swift action, rather than as a partial action (Chapter 7). If it is also Silent and Stilled, the entire spell can therefore be cast as a single swift action, assuming there is no material or focus component.
Metamagic Cost: +2 levels, not subject to Metmagic cost synergy from Silent Spell and Still Spell (synergy from other metamagic applies normally). Those components are often assumed to already be included, resulting in a combined metamagic cost of +4 levels.
Special: This feat can be applied to any spell cast spontaneously (including incarnate spells, sorcerer and bard spells, and divine spells cast spontaneously), without increasing the casting time. Because most incarnates and sorcerers have no material or focus components, this feat is especially useful to them. Bards generally cannot Silence their spells, but have other ways of improving their spellcasting action economy.

sections.heading: Ray SplittingDrAn5 [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can attack multiple targets with a ray spell.
Benefit: This feat functions similarly to Manyshot, but it applies to ray attacks. One ray can instead be used to attack two different targets; each attack takes a -2 penalty to the attack roll. If your base attack bonus is at least +6, you can make iterative attacks as well (or instead of) splitting the ray as described above. For example, a caster with a base attack bonus of +6 could attack with three rays at +4/-1/-1, or with two rays at +4/+4 or +6/+1.
For spells that deal damage, calculate the damage or cap (see Heighten spell, above) as if for a single target, based on the final spell level. Add one die per final level of the spell to the cap, and divide the total among the total number of rays to determine the damage for each ray. For example, scorching ray (essentially, a Split jet of flame) is a 2nd level spell, which has a damage cap of 10d6 against a single target, or a total damage cap of 12d6 for multiple rays. A BAB +6 caster can attack with 2 rays at +6/+1 for 6d6 each, or with 3 rays at +4/+4/-1 for 4d6 each (the latter is similar to the scorching ray spell in the Core rules for a 12th level caster, but with a lower attack bonus). For spells with other numerical effects, add the spell level to the total effect and divide among rays. For example, a split ray of enfeeblement (q.v.; final spell level 2nd) would inflict a total penalty of 1d6+2 +1/2 levels (+12 max.), divided among the rays.If the effect is not numerical, divide the duration instead, again adding the spell level to the total number of units.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.
Synergy: If you also have the Reach Spell feat, you can use it to modify Ray Splitting to allow multiple melee attacks instead, using touch spells (Reach Spell to Close range, making the touch a ray; then apply Ray Splitting; then apply Reach Spell again to reduce the range back to touch).

sections.heading: Special
sections.text: Special: This feat is a specific case of the Cascade Spell feat (q.v.): Warding (resurrection; 1st level) + Accursed Spell (+1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 hr./level; +2 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (those slain by primary spell; -2 levels) = 2nd level.

sections.heading: Reach SpellAPG [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: You can alter a spell to increase its range to a higher range category, using the following order:
# | Range Category | Distance
0 | Touch | 5 ft.
1 | Close | 25 ft. + 5 ft./2 levels
2 | Medium | 100 ft. + 10 ft./level
3 | Long | 400 ft. + 40 ft./level
4 | Extreme | 1,000 ft. + 100 ft./level
5 | Line of Sight | ¼ mile/level
6 | Continental | 100 miles/level
7 | Planar | Anywhere on same plane
8 | Interplanar | Effects reach another plane
Spells modified by this feat that require melee touch attacks instead require ranged touch attacks. Spells and spell-like abilities from other sources with a fixed range of 30 ft. should be treated as “Range: Close” when converted to these rules.
For spells that normally require a line of sight to the target, that requirement is generally waived if the range is Continental or greater. In such cases, the caster must instead have a general idea of the target’s location, and must name or otherwise identify the target.
Metamagic Cost: +/-1 level for each step of increase/decrease (respectively) in range category. For example, a spell with a range of touch increased to long range uses up a spell slot three levels higher:
Reaping SpellCoR [Metamagic]
The dark energy of your spell devours the soul of any creature killed by it.
Prerequisite: Necromancer, or access to Death domain, Graves mystery, Daemon or Undead bloodline, etc.
Benefit: A raise dead, reincarnate, or resurrection spell cannot return to life a creature killed by a reaping spell, and a true resurrection spell has only a 50% chance of succeeding. A reaping spell that fails to kill the target has no additional effect.
Metamagic Cost: +3 spell levels, plus numen cost (150 x CL per victim affected; if you also have the Soulcrafting feat (Chapter 5), you can use the victim’s numen, rather than yours, to pay the maintenance cost).

sections.heading: Reduce Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A reduced spell is less effective than normal:
For spells with a damage or bonus cap, the spell-level-dependent damage cap and/or bonus cap reduced by two spell levels’ worth (1 step on the table). For spells with other Heightening effects that occur on a level-by-level basis (e.g., celerity―see Spell Seeds, below), the effects are reduced by 2 levels’ worth.For spells with other Heightening effects that occur on multiple spell level basis (e.g., zephyr—see Spell Seeds, below), the effects are reduced by 1 step.
These effects supersede any reduction resulting from lowering the spell level due to this feat’s metamagic cost. For example, a 5th level arcane evocation spell (normal damage cap 15d6 for multiple opponents) would have its damage cap reduced to 10d6 if reduced to 4th level (i.e., do not reduce the spell to 4th, read a 10d6 damage cap, and then reduce that again).
This feat cannot be applied to spells that do not improve when Heightened.
Metamagic Cost: -1 level per “step.”
Order of Operations: As with Augment Spell (q.v.), apply this feat after any other metamagic feats that modify the final spell level.
Synergy: When using the Cascade Spell feat (q.v.), there are two additional rules that come into effect:
When a Cascaded spell is Reduced, the reduction occurs to each individual spell in the cascade (as applicable). The metamagic cost discounts do not stack.The minimum final spell level is equal to the lowest cost of the various component spells and their associated metamagic. For example, if you start with a 4th level spell and add Cascade Spell (ray of frost) to increase the level to 5th (for a 15d6 damage cap), you could reduce the spell at most by 1 step (the cost of the ray of frost being added). You could not Reduce Spell to a 5d6 cap (-2 levels instead) for a 3rd level spell, because that would reduce the spell level below its original level before the Cascaded evocation.

sections.heading: Relicguard SpellDr347 [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A relicguard spell does no damage to objects, constructs, or undead.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.

sections.heading: Residual SpellS&T,PnA [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: The area a residual spell affects is considered difficult terrain for 1 round per level of the spell. The exact reason for the difficult terrain depends on the existing terrain and type of spell; explosive spells cast underground might leave rubble; cold spells might leave ice or snow; etc. Athletics checks within the affected area are made at a circumstance penalty equal to the final level of the spell.
Creatures with appropriate favored terrain (e.g., underground for the former example case; arctic for the latter) ignore the difficult terrain created by the spell.
For spells that affect specific targets, rather than an area, on a failed saving throw the affected targets treats all squares as difficult terrain for the duration of the spell.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Resistible Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can be applied only to spells that deal hit point damage (or have some other numerical effect: e.g., ray of enfeeblement) and do not allow a saving throw (e.g., rays and other spells requiring an attack roll). A resistible spell allows a saving throw for half damage or half normal effect.
Metamagic Cost: -1 level.

sections.heading: Restricted Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Game designer (only).
Benefit: A restricted spell is restricted to one very specific spell list and cannot be used by others except by applying the Cross-Class Spell feat (q.v.). Examples might include spells restricted to bards, paladins, or rangers; or spells restricted to a specific cleric domain, incarnate mystery, or sorcerer bloodline bonus spell list; or spells that can be cast only by a specialist wizard of the appropriate school.
Metamagic Cost: -1 level for full or strong progression casters (clerics, druids, incarnates, sorcerers, wizards); -2 levels for poor progression casters (monks, paladins, rangers). If a -2 level adjustment would make the final spell level 0, use a -1 adjustment instead.
Special: This “feat” is included here in order to allow spells to appear on specific, thematically-appropriate spell lists at lower level than would normally be possible. In no event can a character select this feat and apply it to all of his or her spells.

sections.heading: Ricochet Spell [Evocation, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: This feat can only applied to spells with an effect that is a line or a ray (see Area of Effect spells, above). A ricochet spell can be bounced off of walls or other solid barriers. In general, a ranged touch attack against AC 15 is needed in order to hit the barrier in such a way that the spell reflects in the direction desired (a second ranged touch attack to strike the target is also necessary, in the case of rays). Creatures whose spaces are entered twice by a reflected line spell effect are potentially affected twice.
Include all “legs” of the final path when determining the total range the spell has traveled; this cannot exceed the spell’s maximum range.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.
Source: Suggested by the 1st edition D&D lightning bolt spell description.

sections.heading: Ritual Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
By casting a spell as a lengthy ritual, you are able to handle more powerful effects than would normally be possible for you.
Benefit: You can apply this feat only to spells with a casting time of “standard” or 1 round (spells with longer or shorter casting times cannot be affected). By increasing the casting time as shown in the table, you decrease the spell’s effective level.
Metamagic Cost: -1 level to increase casting time from standard to 1 full round (i.e., casting takes an additional partial action). Otherwise -2 levels, with casting times as follows:
Final Level of Spell | Ritual Casting Time
1st – 3rd | 1 minute per final level of spell
4th – 6th | 10 min. per final level of spell
7th – 9th | 1 hour per final level of spell

sections.heading: Ruse SpellUI
sections.text:
Benefit: Attempts to identify a ruse spell by its effects, its aura, its components, or other attributes with a skill check treat the spell as though it were a different spell of the same level or lower. The one attempting the check can correctly identify the spell only by exceeding the DC by 10.
Note that if the ruse spell is disguised as a beneficial spell with a saving throw of (harmless), a willing subject may lose the benefit of a saving throw.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Selective SpellAPG                          [Abjuration, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Your allies need not fear friendly fire.
Benefit: When casting a selective spell with an area effect, you can choose a number of targets in the area equal to your spellcasting attribute modifier. These targets are excluded from the effects of your spell. Spells that do not have an area of effect cannot be modified using this feat.
For spells with duration Instantaneous, the selected targets are simply not affected. For spells with a longer duration, the feat merely provides a 1-round “grace period” during which time the spell does not affect the selected targets—those other than you who remain within the area at the start of your next turn are subject to the effects as if they had entered the area.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level. If you increase the cost to +3 levels, immunity to continuing spell effects lasts the entire duration of the spell, rather than merely 1 round. Regardless of the use of this feat, targets are always subject to effects other than strictly magical ones―such as conjurations produce physical objects (Cf. wall of iron).

sections.heading: Shadow Spell                                                               [Illusion, Metamagic, Shadow]
sections.text:
Your illusions of other spells are partly real.
Prerequisite: Illusionist.
Benefit: Any spell modified with this feat becomes an Illusion [shadow] spell. However, unlike a Phantasmal Spell, for example, the effects are partly real (% real = [final spell level -1] x 10%, minimum 0%).
Spells or creatures that deal damage have normal effects unless the affected creature succeeds on an Intuition save, in which case the damage is multiplied by the fractional reality. If the disbelieved attack (successful Intuition save) has a special effect other than damage, that effect occurs only if the % real score or lower is rolled on percentile dice. Regardless of the result of the save to disbelieve, an affected creature is also allowed any save that the spell or creature being simulated allows. A shadow creature has only the appropriate fraction of the hit points of a normal creature of its kind (regardless of whether it's recognized as shadowy). Furthermore, a disbelieved shadow creature's total AC bonus is fractional.
Metamagic Cost:
For spells originally in the school of Illusion: +1 level For spells originally of other schools: -1 level (+1 level for Cross-Class Spell, in the case of Evocation and Necromancy spells, which are barred spells for Illusionists = +0 levels total).
Synergy: If the spell is prepared, after applying this feat, the final spell can then be Augmented or Reduced (+/-1 level per 10% real, which may make the final value differ from the formula shown above; minimum 0% and max. 90%, and metamagic synergy does not apply).

sections.heading: Shape Spell [Metamagic, Transmutation]
sections.text:
Benefit: You can alter the area of effect to any of the other options on the list (see Area-Effect Spells, above).
Metamagic Cost: Dependent on the change in shape, according to the following table.
Original Shape | New Shape:
Ray | Line | Cone/Wall | Burst etc. | Cube
Ray or target | — | +1 | +2 | +3 | +3
Line | +0 | — | +1 | +2 | +2
Cone or wall | -1 | +0 | — | +1 | +1
Burst, cylinder, or emanation | -2 | -1 | +0 | — | +0
Cubes | -2 | -2 | -1 | +0 | —
Synergy: If the base spell’s area is different than the default for that shape, the new shape is proportionately larger or smaller. For example, a 10-ft. radius burst could be shaped to one 5-ft. cube/level. The Widen Spell feat (q.v.) can then be used to change the final size, if needed.
Source: This feat supersedes the Ray Burst and Ray Coning featsDrAn5, and also the Spellwarp Sniper’s spellwarp prestige class featureCSc.

sections.heading: Shielding Spell [Abjuration, Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Delay Spell.
Benefit: You Delay (q.v.) an offensive spell, setting the activating condition to “when I am hit.” This changes the school of the spell to Abjuration. If the delayed spell is instantaneous, it simply discharges at that time.
Metamagic Cost: +2 level (as Delay Spell with an activating condition of “being hit”).
Synergy:
If you Extend a Shielding spell to last longer, it can instead affect one attacker per round.You can apply the Mass Effect Spell feat (q.v.) to cause the Shielding spell to trigger in response to multiple hits on you; the total number is limited accordingly. If it is also Extended, the Shielding spell affects that number of attackers each round. If the spell normally deals damage, to affect multiple attackers you can either apply the Mass Effect Spell feat (for full damage, as described above), or the Ray Splitting feat. As another alternative, you can affect any number of attackers each round for the duration, but the damage is 1d6 + 1/level (damage cap as shown under Heighten Spell, above).

sections.heading: Silent Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can cast your spells without making any sound.
Benefit: A silent spell can be cast with no verbal components (a partial action is still required to activate the spell, unless the spell is personal or the Quicken Spell feat is also used). Spells without verbal components are not affected.
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.
Special: Bard spells cannot be used in conjunction with this metamagic feat.

sections.heading: Steam SpellARG [Metamagic, Water]
sections.text:
You imbue your [fire] spells with elemental water, transforming them into powerful gouts of steam.
Prerequisite: Access to bloodline, domain, etc. with the [water] descriptor.
Benefit: You infuse a [fire] spell with elemental power, adding the [water] descriptor as well. All fire effects of the altered spell instead manifest as superheated steam, and the altered spell works normally underwater. As the spell still deals fire damage, fire resistance or immunity still applies to the spell's effects.
Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.

sections.heading: Still Spell [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Benefit: A stilled spell can be cast with no somatic components (spells already without somatic components are not affected). A spell with no somatic, focus, or material components can generally be cast as a standard action (Chapter 7).
Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

sections.heading: Sudden MetamagicCA [Metamagic]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Metamagic feat to be affected.
Benefit: Upon gaining this feat, choose one metamagic feat you possess. A number of times per day according to the metamagic cost of the feat, you can apply the effects of that feat to any spell you cast without increasing the level of the spell or specially preparing it ahead of time. Keep track of what the spell level would have been if you had applied the metamagic feat normally; the final spell level thus calculated must be less than or equal to the highest level of spells you can cast.
Base Metamagic Cost | Uses per Day
+1 spell level | 3/day
+2 to +3 spell levels | 2/day
+4 spell levels | 1/day
+5 spell levels or more | —
You can still use the metamagic feat normally.
Special: You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different metamagic feat. Alternatively, you can choose the same feat and gain additional uses per day.

sections.heading: Metamagic Cost
sections.text: Metamagic Cost: +0 levels. In essence, this feat consists of a combination of other metamagic feats: Silent Spell (+1 level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 rd.; -2 levels) = +0 level.

sections.heading: Sudden SpellFOM [Metamagic]
sections.text:
You can cast a spell very quickly at the cost of greatly reduced duration.
Prerequisites: Eschew Materials (or incarnate), Extend Spell, Silent Spell, Still Spell.
Benefit: A Sudden spell is cast as a swift action. You may only use Sudden Spell on a spell with a range of Personal, and only on spells that normally have a duration of at least one minute (ten rounds) when you cast them. The duration of a swift spell is reduced to one round (you cannot subsequently apply the Extend Spell feat to increase this).

sections.heading: Summon, Kindred                                      [Conjuration, Metamagic]
sections.text:
A creature with the Kindred Summon ability can summon other specific creatures of its kind (e.g., demons, devils, etc.) much as though casting a normal summon monster spell, but it usually has only a limited chance of success.
Prerequisite: Summon monster as a racial spell-like ability.
