Save-or-Lose Spells

Many spells that instantly take a combatant out of the fight on a failed save, such as hold person and slay living, have been modified so that they now deal attribute damage, with the condition applying if the attribute is reduced to 0 (Chapter 7, “Conditions”). In this manner, a failed save does not automatically knock a combatant out of the fight, but some debilitating effect occurs even on a successful save. See damage attribute, under “Seed Spells” below, for examples.

Spells that potentially impose permanent conditions (e.g., destruction, insanity, petrifaction) now generally deal attribute drain of the appropriate type. Attribute-draining spells use the damage attribute spell seed and the Crippling Drain metamagic feat (see below).

These sorts of spells are now obviously especially dangerous against creatures whose attribute scores are already reduced through fatigue or exhaustion.

Spell Effect Limitations

In order to cut down the need to track myriad spell effects on characters at high levels, as an optional rule, a character or monster can be affected by a maximum number of spell levels worth of beneficial spells (“buffs”) equal to his or her CR. Buff spells causing this limit to be exceeded have no effect. Permanent spell effects from feats, class features, or bound magic items (Chapter 6) do not count against this limit.

Spell Resistance

Spell resistance can be selectively lowered against specific incoming spells, and then raised again, at will. This does not require an action. If you do not know what spell a dubious ally is casting on you (for example, by using the Spellcraft skill) you must decide blindly whether or not to allow the spell past your SR. An unconscious or dead creature cannot lower spell resistance in this way.

SR more or less follows standardized rules for dispelling magic—i.e., defeating it is an opposed Concentration check. For the sake of ease of play, it can be treated as a passive check, so that the DC of the Concentration check to defeat SR would be equal to 10 + the creature’s Concentration modifier (exclusive of Skill Focus, if any). However, monster hit dice often drastically outstrip CR, so for purposes of SR, the passive check DC is equal to 11 + 3 (class skill) + CR (in place of ranks in Concentration) + the creature’s Charisma modifier.

Spell Subtypes and Descriptors

Most spells, in addition to a school (see below) also receive a subtype—e.g., Conjuration [summoning], or Enchantment [charm]. These are determined by the spell seed(s) (see Seed Spells, below) and cannot be changed except by use of the Cross-Class Spell feat (see Metamagic Feats, below).

It is also possible for spells to have a descriptor―e.g., [acid] or [earth]. Spells dealing energy damage automatically gain the descriptor for that energy type, and some other seed spells provide a descriptor as well (for example, mage armor has the [force] descriptor).

When designing new spells that fit a certain theme, it is possible to add a descriptor appropriate to the theme of the spell. For example, for a spell incorporating the bind and invisible needle seed spells, the effects could be described as entangling pricker vines, and the spell given the [plant] descriptor, making it appropriate for inclusion in the Plant domain list (Cleric Appendix A). A spell dealing bludgeoning damage might be described as a crashing wave (and given the [water] descriptor), or as a smashing rock (and given the [earth] descriptor). For converted pre-published spells, this is assumed to be the case. For spells designed by players, referee permission is needed.

Spells as Weapons

Spells that require an attack roll or touch attack roll, and deal hit point damage, are considered weapons for purposes of applying feats such as Weapon Specialization and Improved Critical. Treat all “touch attack” spells as a weapon group; together, all “ranged touch attack” spells (e.g., rays) get treated as a specific weapon type.

Spells Incompatible with the Revised Rules Framework

Considerable effort has been put into rectifying some of the problems pervasive in 3rd/3.5 edition D&D and Pathfinder. Specific areas addressed include the action economy, the standardized leadership rules (vs. the unfettered control of “magic minions”), limitations on effective caster level and reduced-cost metamagic use, and so on. Spells which violate or undo these corrections are, in general, incompatible with these house rules and should not be used with them. A few examples, with explanations, are provided here.

Arcane FusionCM: Use the Cascade Spell feat instead.

Awaken: This applies a template to the target, so that the mark of the wild rules (see Druid) for control of such a creature are more appropriate than treating the effect as an instantaneous spell.

CelerityPHII: Violates action economy.

Contingency: This spell has been replaced by the Delay Spell feat (q.v.).

Exquisite AccompanymentUM: The revised bard’s “effortless inspiration” class feature already does what this spell is meant to do.

Forced DreamME and WiddershinsRR: In general, spells and powers allowing you to go back in time and redo things represent a forced deus ex machina at best and a game-ender at worst. I do not recommend their use (especially as low as a 3rd level power, in the former case).

Learn Secret, GreaterAUG and Eternal LuckBRL: Use insight and inherent bonus pricing, respectively (Chapter 6) for numen costs.

Masterwork TransformationUM: As written, this spell not only violates masterwork item pricing rules, but also supersedes parts of the Craft skill.

Permanency: Gaining a permanent spell effect requires a feat (Permanent Spell) or investiture of personal numen, not merely the casting of another spell.

Psychic ReformationSRD: Retraining is already permissible, without using powers and paying xp.

Rary’s Arcane ConversionCM: Violates rules of the Variable Spell feat.

ShadowbardUM and Animate InstrumentCSc: Superseded; the revised bard can already begin and maintain inspirations while performing other actions.

Stalker’s SightRR2: The revised ranger can already do this with the quarry ability.

Suffer the FleshME: Violates maximum caster level cap described in Chapter 1.

Two MindsRR: Egregiously violates the revised action economy.

WithdrawUA1: Violates action economy.

Spells that Supersede Skills and Class Features

Invisibility was likewise impossible, at least as far as Flagg himself had been able to determine. Yet it was possible to make oneself… dim. It was necessary to actually hide when one was dim only if one saw someone whom one knew well―for, whether one was dim or not, these people almost always saw. Dimness was useful, but it was not invisibility.

―Stephen King, The Eyes of the Dragon (1987)

There are a number of published spells—both in the core rules and in various supplements—that render skills obsolete and otherwise supersede class features. This has the effect of allowing a caster (or anyone with a wand and the Spellcraft skill) to be a duplicate ranger, rogue, etc. It also severely devalues skills. In these house rules, many of the offending spells are modified or removed, as summarized below.

Searching and Trap-Related Spells: As noted under the detection seed spell, below, the detect secret doors spell is removed from the general wizard’s spell list. All other “automatic search” spells from alternative sources—bypass wardAUG, safe searchBEM3, spontaneous searchDr325, etc.—are removed from their respective standard spells lists and made into rogue skill tricks instead. (Alternatively, a multi-classed rogue/caster with a rogue class level greater than or equal to twice the level of the spell can add that spell back to the appropriate list.)

Spells Providing Bonuses to Skill Checks: These use the skill enhancement seed spell, as shown below and in Appendix 8A; examples include feather stepAPG, freedom of movement, spider climb, and others. In general, skill-enhancing spells and magic items should provide enhancement bonuses, so their effects do not stack. (There are metamagic feats below that allow other bonus types, but these feats also raise the level of the spell.)

Spells That Supersede Class Features: In general, class features should not be easily duplicated by spells. A prime example is find the path; tracking is the ranger’s stock in trade. The effects of the spell are therefore more limited when used by others, as shown under the detection spell seed below. Other examples include:

  • Bestow Grace of the ChampionUM: This spell essentially renders the entire paladin class obsolete.
  • Finding the CenterCA and Solicit PsicrystalSRD: Replace one of the familiar’s primary abilities.
  • ProtégéCAd: Grants bardic inspiration.
  • Vangal’s TouchRR: As written, this spell supersedes barbarian’s primary class feature; however, a modified version (as shown in Appendix C of the Cleric) is permissible.

New Spells: When new sources are introduced, use the above guidelines to evaluate whether to include them. For example, the guiding starAPG and deadeye’s loreUC spells would be restricted to the ranger’s spell list, as they intrude into the ranger’s area of expertise (they are shown this way in Appendix 8A).

Changes to Schools of Magic

The following adjustments are made to specific schools of magic and spells therein.

Abjuration

All personal protective spells other than illusions are designated as Abjuration spells; this includes mage armor and shield. Also, all warding spells on a place or object, and spells modified (via metamagic) to do so, should be moved to the Abjuration school. This includes all forms of magic traps.

Changes to specific spells are summarized below.

Exorcism: Spells such as dispel evil and banishment can be used selectively to affect any undead, outsider, or other spirit possessing (through magic jar, malevolence, etc.) a body. This either banishes the possessing entity (if applicable) or expels it from the host (if not). Likewise, dimensional anchor can be used to trap a possessing spirit in the host’s body.

Warding Spells: Note the numen costs for active or latent spells, described above.

Conjuration

The school of Conjuration loses the [healing] sub-school (which is moved to the school of Necromancy) and also all energy/blasting spells (such as acid splash; these are moved into Evocation instead). It gains blink, ethereal jaunt and etherealness (all of which move the caster to the ethereal plane). Other specific changes are described below.

Feat Requirement: Controlling summoned beings (through summon monster, planar binding, etc.) requires the Thaumaturgy feat, (Chapter 5) which sets CR limits in the manner of the Leadership feat. Without the feat, all summoned extraplanar beings are automatically uncontrolled. Control over a summoned extraplanar being can be broken by dispel magic, greater dispel magic, or break enchantment, requiring a full round action to re-assert control (assuming the thaumaturgist has sufficient CR of control remaining).

It is still possible to bargain with and/or attempt to force uncontrolled outsiders into service, but they will pervert your instructions, undermine your intent, and in general be very hostile to you thereafter unless the payment offered far exceeds the inconvenience and difficulty of the service. This is a specific case in which written guidelines will almost always be insufficient; the referee’s maliciousness and/or perverse amusement are the only limiting factors when dealing with uncontrolled extraplanar beings, so expect the worst.

Summon Monster: Rather than providing lists of allowable summoned monsters, almost any extraplanar creature of the appropriate CR and HD for that spell level can be summoned if the correct spell is known. However, limits on controlled beings (see above) apply; any summoned monsters in excess of your Thaumaturgy allowance are uncontrolled. Prepared summon spells require you to state the being(s) to be summoned as part of the spell preparation, unless the Variable Spell metamagic feat is used (see summon under “Seed Spells,” below).

Summon Nature’s Ally: Summon nature’s allies are controlled through the mark of the wild class feature, rather than the Thaumaturgy feat. They generally share the preparation limitations of summon monster spells. If you cast a summon nature’s ally spell in a specific terrain, you can choose to forego the prepared summons and instead summon a random creature (or number of creatures, if using an Augmented spell) appropriate to that terrain. Doing so prevents any chance of summoning a porpoise into a desert, for example. If cast in a specific terrain that is one of your favored terrains, you can choose the exact creature type(s).

Teleport: Teleportation effects can be blocked by a sufficient thickness of earth or stone, as described under “Castles and Dungeons,” above.

Divination

Divination spells allowing a saving throw call for Intuition saves, rather than Will saves (Chapter 1). In addition, a number of spells within this school have been modified or removed outright; the rationale for many of these changes is given under “Spells that Supersede Skills and Class Features,” above.

Finally, a number of standard detection spells (detect magic, detect secret doors, detect undead) have been either modified or restricted, as noted under those spell descriptions (see Detection spell seed, below)

Read Magic: Rangers, as inveterate explorers, can still cast this spell as a cantrip; for all others, this spell is subsumed by the Knowledge (Linguistics) skill.

Scrying: Scrying effects (including clairvoyance) can be blocked by a sufficient thickness of earth or stone, as described under “Castles and Dungeons,” above.

Enchantment

Spells causing domination, charm, hold effects, and so on generally deal attribute damage or impose attribute penalties, as described under “Save-or-Lose” spells, above. This change affects most of the school of Enchantment; specific examples are provided below (under the damage attribute and ray of enfeeblement seed spells) and in Appendix 8A.

Also note that [charm] effects, as well as confusion and insanity, now call for Intuition saves rather than Will saves (Chapter 1).

Pet Peeve: In game rules language, the word “enchantment” applies strictly to the Enchantment school of magic, and not in any more general sense. Therefore you cannot “enchant” a mindless inanimate object (magic items are “imbued” with properties, not “enchanted” with them).

Evocation

All direct-damage “blasting” spells (e.g., acid splash, orb of force, etc.) are moved into the school of Evocation, including those designated as Conjuration in the 3.5 edition and Pathfinder rules.

The spell construction rules (seed spell + metamagic, described below) makes this one of the most versatile schools. For example, an evoker with the ray of frost spell, the versatile evocation ability, and a few metamagic feats (Reach Spell, Shape Spell) automatically “knows” (can construct) burning hands, cone of cold, and fireball as well (for example), without needing to put them in his spellbooks as separate spells.

Damage caps for evocation spells from the 3.0 edition Dungeon Master’s Guide are retained here, as summarized under “Effects of Heightening Spells,” below.

Illusion

Note that disbelief is now an Intuition save, not a Will save (Chapter 1).

Figments: Most of this sub-school can be built using a basic figment “seed spell” (see below) and metamagic.

Glamers: As with figments, most of this sub-school can be built using a basic glamer “seed spell” (see below) and metamagic.

Simulacrum: Constructing this spell from its component “seeds” and applying the standardized control rules for Leadership-like feats results in substantially less potential for abuse; refer to the simulacrum entry in the spells Grimoire (Appendix 8A).

Necromancy

Controlling Undead: Controlling undead, such as those produced by the animate dead or create undead spells, requires the Command Undead feat (Chapter 5), which functions much like Leadership for undead. If you do not have that feat (or exceed your CR cap), undead that you create or summon are uncontrolled.

Death Spells: These spells now generally deal Constitution damage or drain rather than hit point damage, as described under “Save or Lose Spells,” above. Specific examples are provided under Seed Spells (damage attribute), below.

Gems and Souls: Almost without exception, spells that interact with the soul require gems as material components. For this reason, those particular gems are not in large circulation, and count against the caster’s overflow numen (Chapter 6). The specific types of gems needed, and their values, are as follows:

  • Animate dead, etc.: Onyx or bloodstone worth 25 gp/HD of undead to be animated.
  • Binding, soul bind, trap the soul, etc.: Black sapphire worth 1,000 gp per HD of the creature whose soul is to be trapped. The soul is either trapped within the gem itself, or else the gem is crushed (if the soul is to be consigned to Hell, etc.).
  • Raise dead, resurrection, etc.: Diamond worth (spell level2 x caster level2), rounded up to the nearest multiple of 5,000 gp (e.g., 5,000 gp for a 5th level spell, 10,000 gp for 7th, 25,000 gp for 9th). Generally, the diamond is crushed during the casting.

Healing: The [healing] subschool is moved from Conjuration back into the school of Necromancy (where it was in 1st edition).

This subschool includes spells built using the spark of life and remove condition seeds (see below), which encompasses the cure wounds spells, neutralize poison, remove blindness/deafness, remove disease, the restoration spells, raise dead and resurrection, etc. (This change will please the many people inexplicably clamoring for a “white necromancer” variant.)

Negative Energy Damage: In order to keep the number of energy damage types manageable, desiccation damageSSt, disintegration damage, entropic damage, necrotic damage, etc. can be all treated as negative energy damage. See also ray of entropy under Seed Spells, below.

Restoration: This line of spells works somewhat differently; see Seed Spells (remove condition), below.

Skill Prerequisite: Use of a Necromancy [healing] spell requires a number of ranks in Heal as a class skill equal to twice the level of the spell (round up). In other words, only a character skilled in mundane healing can properly diagnose a problem and heal it with magic.

Transmutation

Because this school in the core rules covers almost any effect imaginable, spells in the existing Transmutation school that could reasonably fit into other schools should be moved accordingly. For example, the etherealness spell, which allows travel to the ethereal plane, should be moved to the Conjuration school; the pyrotechnics spell, which creates a burst of fireworks, should be moved to the Evocation school. This is reflected in the seed spells described below.

Changes to specific Transmutation spells are described below.

Haste: Because of the substantial boosts to martial prowess already inherent in these house rules, haste now specifically affects only one target (see under Celerity seed, below). The Mass Effect spell metamagic feat (q.v.) can be added to create a 6th level mass haste spell.

Mage Hand: No longer targets “only non-magical items,” so that this cantrip cannot do double duty as a ranged detect magic spell as well.

Spells Providing Bonuses to Skill Checks: As noted under “Spells that Supersede Skills and Class Features,” above.

Universal

Contingency: Rather than keeping contingent spells the same level and simply expending another spell slot, contingent spells are handled using the Delay Spell metamagic feat (see below). This means that contingent spells are higher level than non-contingent ones.

Permanency: The permanency spell is removed in favor of the Permanent Spell feat (see below).

Wish: A wish with permanent effects is in essence a continuous spell effect, and requires investment of personal numen accordingly (see Active Spell Effects, above): spell level x caster level x 1,000 x duration multiplier (if applicable). Dominating, forcing, or otherwise coercing another creature into pronouncing the wish for you does not transfer the cost to that creature. If the wish would put you over your maximum numen, it fails or backfires horribly. If you attempt to wish that subsequent wishes not carry this cost, the initial wish fails outright but still carries the numen cost.

It is recommended that the wish spell have the same effects as listed in the CRB, with the following additional uses and exceptions:

  • Create Item: A wish can be used to create any item, mundane or magical. Instead of an active spell effect cost, you spend enough additional numen to bind the item (Chapter 6). If this causes you to exceed maximum, the item remains only so long as you are actively pursuing the current adventure.
  • Inherent Bonuses to Attribute Scores: Attribute scores are not “shuffled,” as in the core rules. Rather, use of a wish to this end costs additional numen as appropriate to an inherent attribute score increase (Chapter 6). Again, this cost supersedes the active spell effect cost for the wish.

Metamagic

A great number of additional metamagic feats, beyond those in the core rules, are presented in here. This is done in hopes of making the “building blocks” of existing higher-level spells more transparent. As noted previously, most if not all published higher-level spells can ideally be treated simply as lower-level spells with appropriate metamagic feats added to them. Specific examples are provided below, and in the Grimoire (Appendix 8A).

Metamagic feats used in tandem, and the Heighten Spell feat in general, work somewhat differently than in 3.5/Pathfinder, as outlined below.

Applying Metamagic

Metamagic can be applied normally: prepared casters must generally prepare the spells in advance in their modified form; spontaneous casters can apply metamagic spontaneously, which always requires a somatic component (but does not otherwise increase the casting time).

There are a few variations and additional options in these house rules, as described below.

Applying metamagic requires a Spellcraft check (Chapter 4) at a DC equal to 15 + the total spell level including metamagic costs (treating +0 costs as +1, and treating negative costs as if they were positive). This restriction does not apply to casting or preparing spells that come pre-modified (see below).

Metamagic Schools: Feats with a school descriptor cannot be used by specialists for whom that particular school is barred, even if the primary school is usable.

Metamagic Synergy: If a spell is modified with a metamagic feat carrying a spell level cost of at least +1, each additional metamagic feat thereafter applied to that spell has its spell level cost, if positive, decreased by 1 (to a minimum of +1). This mechanism, in most cases, allows the final modified spell level to match that in the core rules. For example, a fireball spell is simply a 0-level jet of flame spell, with the Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) and Shape Spell (ray to burst: +3 -1 = +2) feats applied, for a final level of 0 + 1 + 2 = 3rd. Other examples are provided below, and in Appendix 8A.

Pre-Modified Spells: Wizards and archivists might find pre-modified spells that can be scribed into their spellbooks at the appropriate (modified) spell level; this does not require the caster to know the metamagic feat in question. Likewise, a spontaneous caster might gain a spell pre-modified with metamagic directly as a spell known: for example, an incarnate could simply learn maximized searing light as a 5th level spell (with the normal casting time), rather than selecting searing light as a 3rd level spell and also taking the Maximize Spell feat. In this case, neither the unmodified spell nor the metamagic feat (for use on other spells) is available to the caster.

Innate Metamagic: Another option is to select the Innate Metamagic feat (q.v.) and apply it to a spell instead of a spell-like ability, allowing in essence a Sudden Metamagic feat (q.q.v.) usable only with that particular spell, but usable either 3/day (instead of 1/day), or at will with a sufficiently high number of ranks in Concentration. Although far superior to the above option in terms of spell level required, this option requires the expenditure of a feat.

Hero Points and Metamagic Feats: You can use hero points to spontaneously apply any metamagic feat you know without increasing the casting time and without increasing the spell level. For each level by which the spell level would normally be increased, this costs 1 hero point.

Mitigating Metamagic: Some metamagic feats have a negative cost—i.e., they reduce the final level of the modified spell. Negative-cost metamagic, when applied while preparing spells, requires an additional 1 hour per spell level worth of reduction (this does not apply to pre-modified spells). Metamagic feats that reduce the final spell level cannot be applied spontaneously.

Heightened Spells

The effects of Heighten Spell are automatically applied whenever a spell’s level is increased by applying metamagic (e.g., a Maximized acid splash is treated as a 3rd level spell for all purposes, not as a 0-level spell). Heighten Spell can also be applied by itself; this requires a Spellcraft check (DC 20 + final level of the spell).

Metamagic Feats

Unless otherwise noted, all [metamagic] feats in this section are also assumed to have the [arcane] descriptor, in addition to any others listed.

Prerequisites: In addition to the prerequisites listed, learning a metamagic feat requires a number of ranks in Spellcraft equal to 2 x the Metamagic Cost (see below).

Metamagic Cost: The “Metamagic Cost” entry is the increase in spell level that the feat applies to the base spell (e.g., a Metamagic Cost of “+1 level” means that the feat takes up a spell slot 1 level higher than the base spell). In many cases, this can be scaled in order to increase the effects.

“Missing” Feats: Most metamagic feats that directly inflicted a condition (e.g., Dazing Spell, Toppling Spell) are now simulated using Cascade Spell, with the appropriate condition seed spell (see below). The distinction is that spells should do something, whereas metamagic should modify spells.

Accursed Spell [Curse, Metamagic, Necromancy]

Prerequisite: Hex Spell (q.v.).

Benefit: A spell modified by this feat becomes a [curse]. This has several effects:

  • The school of the spell changes to Necromancy.
  • Any penalty it inflicts becomes a profane penalty (regardless of its original type).
  • The saving throw (if applicable) changes to Intuition.
  • The effects cannot be removed by dispel magic (remove curse, break enchantment, etc. are effective).

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Special: To make a curse permanent, you invest personal numen at the time of casting; pricing is as for a latent spell effect (see above), but applying the duration multiplier as for an active effect: spell level x caster level x 50 x duration multiplier. You can also state a deed which, if accomplished, ends the curse (the deed must be possible to be accomplished within 1 year, and help is permissible). If so, contingent pricing is used (Chapter 6), allowing you to ignore the duration multiplier.

Amplify Spell [Metamagic]

Prerequisite: Imbue Item.

Benefit: When placed into an item, an amplified spell functions at the activator’s caster level, rather than at the item’s. In addition, the save DC (if applicable) is calculated using the activator’s Charisma modifier. This feat has no effect on spells that are not imbued into items.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Source: Use this feat for staves, for example, pricing them at the minimum caster level to use the highest-level spell, after applying this feat to each spell. Such items will generally also use the Restricted Spell feat, requiring a particular casting type and level, for a -1 spell level adjustment that offsets the cost of this feat.

Augment Spell [Metamagic]

Benefit: When you Augment a spell that has automatically scaling effects when Heightened, the spell is treated as if it were 1 level higher (if the effects scale by each spell level) or as if 1 “step” higher (if effects scale by a range of levels), for each level by which the spell is Augmented.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level per “step.” This cost is not factored in when determining the base bonus or effects that are then Augmented. When used to increase a spell’s damage cap, this cost is not reduced by metamagic synergy (see above). For example, a 4th level spell dealing 10d6 damage to multiple creatures, if Augmented to 5th level, has a final damage cap of 15d6 (10d6 for being 4th level, +1 step; not 20d6 (15d6 for being 5th level, +1 more step).

Order of Operations: As with Reduce Spell (q.v.), apply this feat after any other metamagic feats that modify the final spell level.

Synergy: When used in conjunction with metemagic feats that lower the final spell level, Augment Spell (to Heighten the effects) is applied after the cost reductions, not before. Therefore, it is not possible, for example, to construct a 0-level spell that has effects as if it were a 5th level spell. For player use, the only exception to this rule is the Restricted Spell feat (q.v.).

Special: Some “seed spells” (see below) can also have other, different improvements when Augmented (as listed for each); unless otherwise noted, those costs can be reduced by metamagic synergy.

Bane Spell [Metamagic]

Benefit: A spell that deals direct damage, when modified by this feat, deals additional damage to one or more types of creatures (examples from the core rules include water elementals and plant creatures; fungi, molds, slimes, oozes, and undead; etc.). Damage against the selected creatures is increased by one die type (e.g., 20d6 becomes 20d8 damage).

Metamagic Cost: +1 level. If the creature type is preselected for the spell when prepared or learned, and cannot be changed by the caster, then the adjustment is +0. You cannot add this feat to a spell more than once, nor can you apply this feat to a spell already modified by the Creature-Specific Spell feat (q.v.).

Special: This is similar to the Bane Magic feat in Chapter 5, but with a spell level adjustment because the creature type can be changed by the user.

Bouncing SpellAPG

[Metamagic, Transmutation]

You can direct a failed spell against a different target.

Benefit: Whenever a bouncing spell targeting a single creature has no effect on its intended target due to spell resistance or a successful saving throw, you may, as a swift action, redirect the full effect to another eligible target within range. The redirected spell behaves in all ways as if its new target were the original target for the spell.

Spells that affect a target in any way (including a lesser effect) on a successful saving throw may not be redirected in this manner, nor can touch spells or spells requiring an attack roll.

Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

Cascade SpellFOM,DMG1 [Metamagic]

Benefit: You can combine two spells into a single cascade spell. The range and area of effect (or target) of the cascade spells are equal to the lesser of those of the two spells. For cascaded spells with different durations, those durations can be tracked separately, or combined into a single duration equal to the lesser of the two. Casting time is equal to the longer of the two casting times. The cascaded spell requires all of the components listed for each of the constituent spells. In addition:

  • Damage caps and other Heightening effects (see above) are determined by final spell level, not for individual spells within a Cascade.
  • When cascading spells of different schools, neither can be a barred school for the caster, or else the entire spell fails.

Once the two spells have been Cascaded, they are thereafter treated as a single spell, and can be modified as a unit using other metamagic feats (e.g., after being Cascaded together, two touch-range spells can be converted to a ray with a single application of the Reach Spell feat). An exception is if separate durations were maintained.

For purposes of specialist wizard, a cascade spell with one component in the specialist school is treated as a specialist school spell (but barred school restrictions for the other component spell(s) still apply).

Metamagic Cost: A cascade spell uses up a spell slot one level higher than the total level of both spells in the cascade. Adding a spell to an existing spell always results in at least a +1 spell level increase; you cannot start with a low-level spell, add negative level-cost metamagic, and then Cascade that onto an existing spell with the net effect of lowering the other spell’s level. There are other specific rules when using Reduce Spell (q.v.) in conjunction with this feat.

Synergy: It is not possible to Cascade multiple damage-inflicting spells together in order to inflict total damage greater than the (final) level-based damage caps shown under Effects of Heightening Spells, above. To deal multiple types of damage, the Energy Admixture feat (see above) is used instead.

Special: In some of the example spells from the Grimoire, a Cascaded spell that adversely affects the caster is included, with a negative metamagic cost equal to the level of the Cascaded spell (this applies only if the Cascaded spell is appropriately dangerous or harmful to the caster, per the referee’s discretion). This simulates the “corruption cost” of Corrupt spellsBVD,HH.

Channel Spell [Metamagic]

Benefit: A channeled spell can be discharged through a weapon attack. This otherwise works as a touch spell (in terms of casting and Holding the Charge); the only difference is in the delivery. The next time you strike an opponent with that weapon, the spell discharges. The target takes the normal damage and effects of a successful attack in addition to the spell's effect.

You can place a channeled spell on a piece of ammunition or a projectile, such as a sling bullet, an arrow, or a crossbow bolt. In such a case, the spell dissipates if the attack misses. The spell cannot be placed on a bow, crossbow, sling, or similar weapon that uses ammunition.

If the weapon is an eldritch blast (or other similar attack ability), only the creature struck is affected, even if the spell normally affects multiple targets or an area. Only if the eldritch blast itself is modified to affect an area (as with the Shape Spell feat) or multiple targets (as with the Ray Splitting feat) can a channeled spell affecting an area or multiple targets do so. Likewise, if the spell normally affects only a single target, but the eldritch blast or other ability affects multiple targets or an area, then the spell applies to only one of the targets within the area of effect.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level. You cannot use the Manifested Spell feat (q.v.) in order to defray this cost.

Synergy:

  • In order to Channel a spell into multiple attacks, also apply the Ray Splitting feat (q.v.).
  • If you Extend (q.v.) an instantaneous Channeled spell, the weapon used to channel the spell can be used throughout that time period—i.e., it becomes, in essence, a temporary magic item.

Special: In some cases, this feat can be used to channel a spell through some object or manifestation other than a weapon—Cf. project image in Appendix 8A.

Source: Smiting SpellPHII. This feat also supersedes the Eldritch Theurge’s spellblast and greatreach blast prestige class featuresCM.

Coaxing SpellPC [Metamagic]

Prerequisite: Profession (mining) 1 rank or favored terrain: underground (for oozes); or Survival 1 rank (for plants and vermin).

Benefit: This feat works only on [mind-affecting] spells, and spells inflicting other effects to which oozes, plants, and/or vermin are normally immune. A coaxing spell affects those creature types despite their normal immunity, but other creature types are immune. Cf. Threnodic Spell (q.v.).

Metamagic Cost: +0 levels. If you increase the cost to +2 levels (essentially removing the implied “Creature-Specific Spell” metamagic of this feat), the spell affects other targets normally.

Normal: Oozes, plants, and vermin are immune to [mind-affecting] spells and effects, and to attribute penalties, damage, and drain.

Communal SpellUC [Metamagic]

Benefit: The effects of a communal spell can be applied to any willing creatures. However, the total duration is divided as evenly as possible among the recipients you select, in increments equal to the duration’s time units (rounds, minutes, hours, etc.). Any unused duration is wasted.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Concentration Spell [Metamagic]

With concentration, you can maintain spells beyond their normal durations.

Prerequisite: Extend Spell.

Benefit: The duration of a Concentration Spell is equal to the length of time you concentrate, plus the spell’s normal duration thereafter. Concentrating to maintain a spell generally requires a standard action, and you must succeed at a Concentration check (DC 10 + twice the level of the spell) to maintain concentration on it. Anything that could break your concentration when casting a spell (e.g., you are threatened and fail to cast defensively, or take damage) can also break your concentration while you're maintaining one, causing the spell to end.

For spells that would normally have an instantaneous duration, you can redirect the effect once per round, for as long as you concentrate. For area-effect spells, you can move the effect up to 30 ft. per round. Any portion of the area that would extend beyond your maximum range dissipates harmlessly, reducing the remaining area thereafter. Because the effect is re-directed from round to round, it does not count as continuing damage for purposes of forcing Concentration checks (Chapter 4) from those affected.

Metamagic Cost: +2 levels. By increasing the cost, you can maintain a Concentration spell more efficiently:

  • Partial action: +3 levels;
  • Swift action: +4 levels.

Consecrate SpellCD [Divine, Good, Metamagic]

Prerequisite: Any [good] alignment.

Benefit: This feat adds the [good] descriptor to a spell and may have an additional effect:

  • If the spell deals damage, half of the damage (rounded down) is holy damage resulting directly from divine power, and is therefore not subject to be reduced by resistance or immunity to energy-based attacks.
  • If the spell provides a numerical bonus, the bonus type changes to [sacred].

Note that arcane spells generally cannot be modified with this feat.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Corrupt SpellCD [Divine, Evil, Metamagic]

Prerequisite: Any [evil] alignment.

Benefit: This feat adds the [evil] descriptor to a spell. If the spell deals damage, half of the damage (rounded down) is unholy damage resulting directly from divine power, and is therefore not subject to be reduced by resistance or immunity to energy-based attacks. If the spell provides a numerical bonus, the bonus type changes to [profane].

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Prerequisite: Game designer (only)—not for PCs.

For example, a cleric could imbue a fighter companion with a permanent +3 sacred bonus to attacks and damage (by means of an Extended divine favor spell); the fighter would have to select Permanent Spell as a feat in order to gain this effect. For example, a caster with a base attack bonus of +6 could attack with three rays at +4/-1/-1, or with two rays at +4/+4 or +6/+1.

  • For spells that deal damage, calculate the damage or cap (see Heighten spell, above) as if for a single target, based on the final spell level. For example, scorching ray (essentially, a Split jet of flame) is a 2nd level spell, which has a damage cap of 10d6 against a single target, or a total damage cap of 12d6 for multiple rays. A BAB +6 caster can attack with 2 rays at +6/+1 for 6d6 each, or with 3 rays at +4/+4/-1 for 4d6 each (the latter is similar to the scorching ray spell in the Core rules for a 12th level caster, but with a lower attack bonus).
  • For spells with other numerical effects, add the spell level to the total effect and divide among rays. For example, a split ray of enfeeblement (q.v.; final spell level 2nd) would inflict a total penalty of 1d6+2 +1/2 levels (+12 max.), divided among the rays.

Reduce Spell [Metamagic]

Benefit: A reduced spell is less effective than normal:

  • For spells with a damage or bonus cap, the spell-level-dependent damage cap and/or bonus cap reduced by two spell levels’ worth (1 step on the table).
  • For spells with other Heightening effects that occur on a level-by-level basis (e.g., celerity―see Spell Seeds, below), the effects are reduced by 2 levels’ worth.
  • For spells with other Heightening effects that occur on multiple spell level basis (e.g., zephyr—see Spell Seeds, below), the effects are reduced by 1 step.

These effects supersede any reduction resulting from lowering the spell level due to this feat’s metamagic cost. For example, a 5th level arcane evocation spell (normal damage cap 15d6 for multiple opponents) would have its damage cap reduced to 10d6 if reduced to 4th level (i.e., do not reduce the spell to 4th, read a 10d6 damage cap, and then reduce that again).

This feat cannot be applied to spells that do not improve when Heightened.

Metamagic Cost: -1 level per “step.”

Order of Operations: As with Augment Spell (q.v.), apply this feat after any other metamagic feats that modify the final spell level.

Synergy: When using the Cascade Spell feat (q.v.), there are two additional rules that come into effect:

  • When a Cascaded spell is Reduced, the reduction occurs to each individual spell in the cascade (as applicable). The metamagic cost discounts do not stack.
  • The minimum final spell level is equal to the lowest cost of the various component spells and their associated metamagic. For example, if you start with a 4th level spell and add Cascade Spell (ray of frost) to increase the level to 5th (for a 15d6 damage cap), you could reduce the spell at most by 1 step (the cost of the ray of frost being added). You could not Reduce Spell to a 5d6 cap (-2 levels instead) for a 3rd level spell, because that would reduce the spell level below its original level before the Cascaded evocation.

Such creatures include ethereal creatures, creatures that are blinking or shadow walking, manifested ghosts, and creatures within the extradimensional space of a rope trick, portable hole, or familiar pocket. You must be able to perceive a creature to target it with a transdimensional spell, but you do not need to perceive a creature to catch it in the area of a burst, cone, emanation, or spread.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level. If the spell only affects incorporeal creatures and not material ones, the level cost is instead -1, as if the Creature-Specific Spell feat (q.v.) had also been applied.

Normal: Only ghost touch or [force] spells and effects can affect ethereal creatures, and no Material Plane attack affects creatures on the Plane of Shadow or in an enclosed extradimensional space. Spells other than [force] effects deal 50% damage against incorporeal creatures.

Source: This feat subsumes the Ectoplasmic Spell featAPG.

Unskittering Spell [Evocation, Metamagic]

Your knowledge of arcane defenses allows you to cast spells that bypass them.

Benefit: This feat can be applied only to spells that require an attack roll (melee or ranged; normal or touch). An unskittering spell ignores deflection bonuses to AC and CMD, and also ignores any AC bonus granted by mage armor or bracers of armor.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Source: This is the “Piercing Spell” home brew feat from the angelfire Migdalia campaign.

Variable Spell [Metamagic, Transmutation]

Prerequisite: At least two other metamagic feats.

Benefit: For spells with multiple parameters that are selected when the spell is learned or prepared, this feat instead allows the selection of those parameters at the time of casting. Examples are provided below and in Appendix 8A.

For spells prepared with metamagic, or that come pre-modified, a variable spell has a menu of specific metamagic feats (including Cascaded spells, q.v.) or combinations of feats, created when the spell is prepared or created. Each feat or combination of feats in the menu must have the same total metamagic cost. At the time of the casting, one of these options is selected by the caster.

All of the options use the same base spell as the root, and they must all follow a relatively narrow theme or motif (referee and player agreement). It is thus not possible to use this feat to prepare, in essence, large numbers of potential 5th level spells in place of one 6th level spell.

Metamagic Cost: +1 level.

Synergy: For spells extended using the Concentration Spell feat (q.v.), a different menu option can be selected each round.

Special: In a few example spells (notably confusion), the Variable Spell feat has been applied at a -1 spell level cost, because the caster has no control over which menu option that will apply. This use of the feat is generally for Game Designer use only (Cf. Restricted Spell).

Violate SpellBVD [Evil, Metamagic, Necromancy]

The wounds the spell inflicts are tainted with the foulest evil.

Prerequisite: Corrupt Spell (q.v.); evil alignment.

Benefit: This feat adds the [evil] descriptor to the modified spell. Furthermore, if the spell deals hit damage, half of the damage dealt is Vile damage, which can only be healed by healing or restoration magic that is cast within an area sanctified by the forces of good (such as within a consecrate or a hallow spell). Natural healing, regeneration, fast healing and magical healing are otherwise ineffective in restoring the lost hit points or ability points.

Metamagic Cost: +2 levels.

Volumetric BurstPH1 [Evocation, Metamagic]

Prerequisite: Shape Spell.

Benefit: When this feat is applied to a spell with a “burst” or “spread” area of effect, the spell effects always fill the full (normal) volume of space. Each square that an affected spell is prevented from occupying (because of a wall or similar obstruction) is added to the other side of the effect's area. For example, a fireball normally bursts in a 20-ft. radius (1,255 square feet, or 50 squares). When used in a long, 10-ft.-wide hallway, a volumetric fireball would occupy 125 feet of the corridor’s length (the target pair of squares, plus 12 pairs of squares in either direction along the length of the hallway). If cast in a totally confined area less than or equal to half the total volume (for example, a fireball cast within a closed 20-ft. x 20-ft. room), the spell deals double damage/effects to everyone within the area.

Metamagic Cost: +0 levels.

Seed Spells

Ideally, almost all spells can be “built” using a low-level basic “seed” spell and metamagic feats. The system outlined herein is designed to that end. As a general rule of thumb, if an existing spell can be built using seed spell(s) and metamagic feats, then do so; if not, it can potentially be used as-is (with referee permission) provided that it does not violate any of the strictures noted in above. A large number of existing spells have been so converted, and are presented in Appendix 8A.

Most seed spells can be Augmented for greater effects. Each augmentation is essentially a metamagic feat (q.v.) that applies to that spell, and follows the general rules for metamagic feats described above. However, rather than learning each Augmentation as a separate feat, a caster who knows the base spell can apply the Augmentation when preparing the spell. Spontaneous casters can apply the Augmentation during casting by succeeding at a Spellcraft check (as if for Heightening the spell; DC 20 + final level of the spell).

Special: In some of the example cases presented here, the metamagic rules have been stretched somewhat so as to allow a given spell to be reproduced without the need for creating an excessive number of new metamagic feats, etc. When the spell creation rules are used within an ongoing game, they should be followed as written unless the participants agree on a specific variation being permissible.

Existing Spells: The following spells can be used “as-is,” without being built from other seeds: contagion (reduce spell level to 2nd), unseen servant. In addition, most cantrips can be used as written, treating them as minor variations of prestidigitation.

Description Your life force occupies the host body. The host's soul is imprisoned with you, but can still use its own senses (though it can't assert any influence or use even purely mental abilities unless you allow it). You can communicate telepathically with the host as if you shared a common language, but only with your consent. You keep your mental attributes, class levels and class features, BAB, base save bonuses, and mental abilities. The body retains its physical attributes, hp, natural abilities, and automatic abilities. A body with extra limbs doesn't allow you to make more attacks (or more advantageous two-weapon attacks) than normal.

You can use your own spells and spell-like abilities, but a totally unnatural form for you (e.g., a human caster possessing an aberration, animal, etc.) would require you to apply the Natural Spell feat. You can't activate the body's supernatural abilities, nor can you cast any of its spells or spell-like abilities (although the host can, if you allow it and use the body to perform the needed components).

When you transfer your soul upon casting, your body appears to be dead. Failure to take over a host ends the spell. If the possession succeeds, as a standard action, you can shift freely back to your own body regardless of range, so long as it remains on the same plane. If the host's body is killed, you return to your own body and the life force of the host departs (it is dead). If your body is slain, when the spell expires or the host's body is killed, you are slain. It is possible to cast this spell on a new target from within another creature's body. You still return to your original body (not any intermediate body) when you take a standard action to do so or the spell's duration expires. Returning to your body ends the spell.

Casters whose souls are their bodies, such as incorporeal undead, fey, and non-native outsiders, use the effects of greater possessionOcA instead (see below), and incorporeal undead and evil outsiders can possess dead bodies as if they were still alive.

Ch 8a - Spells Grimoire

Appendix 8a: Spells Grimoire

This appendix contains examples of spells from the core rules and other sources, rebuilt using seed spells and metamagic. They include the synergy effects of metamagic stacking, and also the automatic Heighten Spell effects of applied metamagic, as described in Chapter 8.

Generally, the spell effects and calculated spell level are very similar (or identical) to those described in the source material. In the event of a variance, a “listed as” reference may be provided; this indicates the spell level listed in the source, for comparison with the calculated spell level.

In many cases, a number of spells from different sources have different names, but similar or nearly identical effects (e.g., sanctuary alone has at least 13 variants). In order to save space (and to avoid excessive cross-indexing), rather than all of them receiving separate entries, one of the spells is listed alphabetically, and the variations are described as bullet points at the end of that entry. Therefore, a Search function may be needed to find a specific spell, if it does not appear alphabetically in the document.

Spells named after a deity, wizard, etc. (e.g., Mordenkainen’s sword) are alphabetized with the proper name last (e.g., “Sword, Mordenkainen’s”).

Note that a number of feats and class features with spell-like effects have also been converted here as spells. To use them as feats, simply select them in conjunction with the Magical Talent feat (Chapter 5).

Aid PlantsAUG: Warding (disease; 1st level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +3 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 1,000’r.; +5 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (nonintelligent, inanimate plants; -2 levels) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 rd./level; -1 level) + Ritual Spell (-2 levels) + Resticted Spell (access to Plant domain; -1 level) = 3rd level (listed as 2nd); plants in large area resist disease: invest 200 x CL numen (as latent spell) to maintain effect.

Alarm: Variable Spell (see below; +1 level):

  • Mental alarm: MindlinkSRD (1st level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 rd.; -2 levels) = -1 level; or

+ Delay Spell (creature enters 20’r. area or touches object without saying password; +1 level) + Tenacious Spell (+1 level) + Ritual Spell (full round; -1 level) = 1st level.   • Attentive alarmCM: Alarm (q.v.; 1st level) – Variable Spell (mental only; -1 level) + Cascade Spell (detection; +3 levels) = 3rd level; as mental alarm, and you know the type and numbers of the creatures that trigger the alarm.
  • Cacophonous AlarmCM: Alarm (q.v.; 1st level) – Variable Spell (audible only; -1 level) + Cascade Spell (sound lance; +1 level) + Cascade Spell (inertia; +1 level) + Augment Spell (daze; +2 levels) + Reduce Spell (15d6 to 10d6; -1 level) = 3rd level (bard 2nd); as audible alarm, but creature triggering it also takes 1d6 sonic/level (max. 10d6) and is dazed 1 rd. (Fort half/neg.).
  • Greater AlarmSC: Alarm (q.v.; 1st level) + Trans-dimensional Spell (+1 level) = 2nd level; as alarm, but also triggered by creatures on coterminous planes. AKA improved alarmMP.
  • Guarded HearthAPG: Alarm (q.v.; 1st level) + Cascade Spell (resistance; +1 level) + Cascade Spell (blessing; +1 level) + Augment Spell (+2 levels) + Delay Spell (+1 level) + Location-Specific Spell (bonuses apply only within alarmed area; -2 levels) + Mass Effecr Spell (1/3 levels; +2 levels) + Ritual Spell (full round to full ritual; -1 level) + Restricted Spell (access to Community domain; -1 level) = 4th level; area is warded with alarm and those within gain +4 to attacks, damage, and saves for 1 min./level after activated.
  • Invisibility AlarmACG: Alarm (q.v.; 1st level, with delay trigger specifying an invisible creature) + Variable Spell (different alarm, depending if entering or leaving; +1 level) = 2nd level.
  • Mental AlarmAUG2: Figment (0 level) + Delay Spell (time delay; +2 levels) + Phantasmal Spell (-1 level) + Mass Effect Spell (1 creature/level; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to inst.; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (audible only; -3 levels) = 0 level; 1 creature/level hears instantaneous illusionary alarm at end of specified time period.

  • Mordenkainen’s Faithful HoundSRD: Alarm (q.v.; 1st level) + Cascade Spell (invisible needle; +1 level) + Manifested Spell (-1 level) + Channel Spell (through the alarm; +1 level) + Extend Spell (inst. to 1 rd./level; +2 levels) + Irresistible Spell (+2 levels) + Reduce Spell (15d6 to 10d6; -1 level) = 5th level; intrusion triggers loud barking and 1 attack/rd. for 10d6 piercing (no SR) within Close range of it.   • Touch of GracelessnessAPG: Ray of clumsiness (1st level) + Cascade Spell (topple; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) = 1st level; 1d6 + ½ levels (+5 max.) penalty to Dex and fall prone; Fort half/neg.
  • Unprepared CombatantUM: Ray of clumsiness (1st level) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 min./level; +1 level) + Effect-Specific Spell (penalty applies only to Initiative and Reflex saves; -1 level) + Resistible Spell (-1 level) = 1st level; imposes 1d6 +1/2 levels (+5 max.) penalty to Dex, for purposes of determining Initiative and Reflex saves (save neg.).
  • Wardaway7S: Blessing (0 level) + Hex Spell (+0 levels) + Reach Spell (touch to close; +1 level) + Extend Spell (10 min./level to 1 min./level; -1 level) + Cascade Spell (ray of clumsiness; +1 level) + Cascade Spell (celerity; +1 level) + Quicken Spell (+3 levels) + Interrupting Spell (+1 level) + Effect-Specific Spell (Dex penalty to initiative only; -2 levels) + Effect-Specific Spell (charging speed only; -2 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 rd.; -1 level) = 1st level; immediate ranged touch makes target -1 to attacks and damage, treat Dex as 1d6 +1/2 levels lower for determining Initiative, and charge as if its speed were 10 ft. slower.

Bull’s Strength: Attribute boost (Str; 0 level) + Silent Spell (+1 level) + Augment Spell (+2 to +4; +1 level) = 2nd level; subject gains +4 enhancement to Strength for 1 min./level. Variants:

  • Gaean strengthRRO is Augmented (+10 total; +3 levels), Extended (1 hr./level; +2 levels), Location-Specific (standing barefoot on earth or unworked stone; -2 levels), Personal (-1 level), and Ritual (full round; -1 level) = 3rd level; you gain +10 to Str for 1 hr./level, as long as remain standing barefoot (or lying down) on bare earth or unworked rock.
  • Giant’s mightRRE Cascades attribute boost (Con; +1 level), is not Silent (-1 level), and is Augmented (+8 total; +2 levels) and Extended (1 min./level to 10 min./level; +1 level) = 5th level; +8 enhancement to Str and Con for 10 min./level.
  • Might of the GodsCRB: Enhancement (2nd level) + Effect-Specific Spell (Str checks and Str-based skill checks; -2 levels) + Augment Spell (+4 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) + Restricted Spell (access to Strength domain; -1 level) = 2nd level; swift casting gives you +1/2 levels to Str checks and Str-based skill checks for 1 rd.
  • Mighty strengthDG is Augmented (+8 total; +2 levels) and Personal (-1 level) = 3rd level (listed as 4th).
  • Oliphaunt’s strengthRRE is Augmented (+6 total; +1 level), Extended (10 min./level; +1 level), and Ritual (full round; -1 level) = 3rd level; +6 enhancement to Str for 10 min./level.
  • Strength of KadumRR is Augmented to +16 (+6 levels) = 8th level.
  • Strength of oneTM2 is Communal rather than Silent, and is Augmented (+8 total; +2 levels) and Restricted (access to Community or Strength domain; -1 level) = 3rd level; up to 1 subject/level gains +8 enhancement to Str for 1 minute each.
  • Strength of NalthalosDD is Augmented (+6 total; +1 level), Extended (1 min./level to 1 hr./level; +2 levels), and Restricted (access to Artifice or Strength domain; -1 level) = 4th level.
  • Strength of stoneS&M is Augmented (+6 total; +1 level), Extended (1 min./level to 1 rd./level; -1 level), and Restricted (access to Earth domain; -1 level) = 1st level.
  • Strength of the tideRRO Cascades attribute boost (Dex; +1 level), is not Silent (-1 level), and is Augmented (+6 total; +1 level), Extended (10 min./level; +1 level), and Restricted (access to Water domain, etc.; -1 level) = 3rd level; +6 enhancement to Str and Dex for 10 min./level.
  • Strength surgeCRB is Extended (1 rd.; -2 levels) and Restricted (access to Strength domain; -1 level) = 0 level; touch grants +6 enhancement to Str for 1 rd.
  • Wyrm’s strengthRRE Cascades attribute boost (Con; +1 level), is not Silent (-1 level), and is Augmented (+12 total; +4 levels) = 6th level; +12 enhancement to Str, +6 to Con for 1 min./level.

Bully’s CurseAUG2: Compel (make no AoOs; 2nd level) + Cascade Spell (blessing; +1 level) + Augment Spell (+3 total bonus; +1 level) + Cascade Spell (deflection; +1 level) + Hex Spell (+0 levels) + Accursed Spell (+1 level) + Reach Spell (touch to medium; +1 level) + Creature-Specific Spell (applies only vs. foes with lower attack bonus; -2 levels) = 5th level (listed as 4th); victim is -3 to attacks and damage, -2 to AC, and cannot make attacks of opportunity when fighting opponents with a lower attack bonus than his own. Invest 500 x CL numen to maintain effect longer than 1 min./level.

BungleUM: Enhancement (2nd level) + Hex Spell (+0 levels) + Reach Spell (touch to close; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 rd.; -2 levels) + Delay Spell (next effort; +1 level) + Creature-Specific Spell (humanoid; -2 levels) + Expedient Spell (individual HD; -1 level) + Augment Spell (+1 to +1/2; +3 levels) = 2nd level (listed as 1st); one humanoid with 6 HD or less takes a -1/2 levels penalty to attacks, saves, or checks for 1 rd., starting when next attempts one.

Buoyancy NetRR: Mage hand (0 level) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) + Widen Spell (1 lb./level to 216 lbs./level; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (conc. to 1 rd./level; +1 level) + Location-Specific Spell (in liquid; -2 levels) + Effect-Specific Spell (float to surface only; -2 levels) = 1st level; causes up to 216 lbs./level of creatures and/or objects to ascend to the surface. Variants:

  • BuoyancyACG is Quickened (+3 levels) = 4th level (listed as 2nd).
  • Otiluke’s Bubbling BuoyancyCA lasts 10 min./level (+2 levels) but affects only 26 lbs./level (-1 level) and requires a full-round casting (-1 level) = 1st level.
  • Wave BlessingSW is Quickened (+3 levels) and Interrupting (+1 level), and lasts 10 min./level (+2 levels) = 7th level (listed as 1st).

Burden of FaithRR2: Ray of enfeeblement (1st level) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to burst; +2 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 min./level; +1 level) + Effect-Specific Spell (carrying capacity only; -2 levels) + Selective Spell (+1 level) + Augment Spell (+15 to +20; +1 level) = 5th level; divine casters (clerics, archivists, incarnates, paladins) in area take penalty to Str (for encumbrance purposes only) of 1d6 + 1/level (Fort half).

Burning BloodCA: Jet of flame (0 level) + Energy Admixture (acid; +0 levels) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) + Cascade Spell (inertia; +1 level) + Augment Spell (staggering; +1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd. to 1 rd./level; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to long; +1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 10d6 (half fire, half acid) plus 2d6/round and staggered 1 rd./level.

  • Burning Blood, Beltyn’sUnE: Acid splash (0 level) + Energy Admixture (fire; +0 levels) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) + Extend Spell (inst. to 1 rd./level; +2 levels) = 3rd level (listed as 5th); damage cap 10d6 (half acid, half fire; Fort half) to same creature each round.

Burning BrandToB: Metaphysical feat (Versatile Evocation: fire; 1st level) + Cascade Spell (bestow feat: Lunge; +2 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 min./level; +1 level) + Object-Specific Spell (melee weapon; -2 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) = 1st level (listed as 2nd); swift casting causes your melee weapon to deal fire damage instead of damage of its normal type for 1 rd., and you can extend its reach by 5 ft.

Burning Hands: Jet of flame (0 level) + Silent Spell (+1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to cone; +1 level) + Widen Spell (30 ft. to 15 ft.; -1 level) = 1st level; damage cap 5d6 fire (Reflex half) in a 15-ft. cone. Variants:

  • Blast of flameCA is Widened to 60 ft. (+2 levels), Irresistible (+2 levels), and Reduced (15d6 to 10d6; ­1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 10d6 fire (no SR) in 60-ft. cone. Dragon’s flameToB is similar, but affects a 30-ft. cone (3rd level; listed as 5th)
  • Deadly laharCM Cascades slow (+3 levels), and is Lingering (+2 levels) and Widened (60 ft.; +2 levels) = 8th level; damage cap 20d6 fire plus staggered and entangled 1 rd./level and 5d6 burn.
  • Fanning the flamesRR2 is long range (+1 level), Widened (60 ft.; +2 levels), and Location-Specific (cone must extend from existing fire source; -2 levels) = 2nd level; damage cap 5d6 fire in 60-ft. cone extending in any direction from an existing fire within Long range.
  • Hatchling’s flameToB is Irresistible (+2 levels), affects a 30-ft. cone (+1 level), and is Reduced (15d6 to 5d6; ­2 levels) = 2nd level; damage cap 5d6 fire (no SR). Wyrm’s flameToB is similar, but is reduced 1 less step (3rd level, listed as 8th; damage cap 10d6).
  • Incendiary surgeCM is Penetrating instead of Silent (+0 levels), affects a 30-ft. cone (+1 level), and is Empowered (+1 level) and Concentration (standard; +1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 1.5 x 10d6 and +2 to penetrate SR; can cast 1/rd. as long as you concentrate.
  • Screaming flamesHA Cascades damage attribute (Wis; +2 levels) = 3rd level; 5d6 fire plus 1d4 Wis in 15-ft. cone.
  • Steam breathCA is Lingering (+1 level) and affects a 30-ft. cone (+1 level) = 3rd level; damage cap 10d6 fire plus 2d6 burn.

Burning HateDr347: Jet of flame (0 level) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) + Cascade Spell [(blessing; +1 level) + Mass Effect Spell (1 creature/level; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (10 min./level to 1 rd./level; -2 levels)] = 2nd level; damage cap 5d6 fire (arcane 10d6; Reflex half), and you and allies (up to 1 per level) gain +1 to attacks and damage against victim for the next 1 rd./level.

Burning SightRR2: Darkvision (q.v.; 2nd level) + Reach Spell (touch to planar; +6 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (individual represented by focus doll; -2 levels) + Ritual Spell (-2 levels) = 5th level (listed as 2nd); grant subject darkvision from anywhere on the same plane.

Burst of AdrenalineOcA: Attribute boost (0 level) + Variable Spell (Str, Dex, or Con; +1 level) + Augment Spell (+8 total bonus; +3 levels) + Cascade Spell (touch of fatigue; -1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) = 2nd level; you gain swift +8 enhancement to one physical attribute and are then fatigued 1 round.

Burst of InsightOcA: Attribute boost (0 level) + Variable Spell (Int, Wis, or Cha; +1 level) + Augment Spell (+8 total bonus; +4 levels) + Effect-Specific Spell (attribute or skill check only; -2 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) + Interrupting Spell (+1 level) + Cascade Spell (inertia; -1 level) + Augment Spell (stagger; -1 level) = 1st level; you gain immediate +8 enhancement to one mental attribute (for purposes of a skill check or attribute check only) and are then staggered 1 rd.

Burst of SpeedUC:

(0 level) + Cascade Spell (skill enhancement: Acrobatics; +1 level) + Cascade Spell (bestow feat: Mobility; +1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 min./level; +1 level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) = 3rd level; you gain +30 ft. to speed, +1/2 levels (+10 max.) to Acrobatics, and the Mobility feat for 1 rd. as a swift action.

Buzzing Bee, Mordenkainen’sMH: Skill enhancement (Concentration; 0 level) + Cascade Spell (skill enhancement: Stealth; +1 level) + Hex Spell (+0 levels) + Reach Spell (touch to medium; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) = 2nd level (listed as 1st); subject is -1/2 levels (-5 max.) to Concentration and Stealth for 1 min./level. Note that in order to force concentration checks simply to cast, and deny a saving throw or SR (as listed), the spell level would be 9th, rather than 1st.

Bypass WardAUG: Warding (magical traps; 1st level) + Reach Spell (touch to close; +1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 rd./level; -1 level) + Restricted Spell (access to Rune domain or rogue skill trick; -1 level) = 2nd level; magical traps (latent spells that trigger when area entered or item disturbed) are suppressed in 20’r. for 1 rd./level.

Cackling SkullUM: Magic mouth (q.v.; 2nd level) + Cascade Spell (spook; +1 level) + Shape Spell (target to spread; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 60’r.; +2 levels) + Object-Specific Spell (must be cast on focus skull; -2 levels) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Reduce Spell (frightened to shaken; -1 level) = 3rd level; pre-recorded speech also causes listeners in 60’r. to be shaken 1 rd./level (save each round to end effect).

Cacophonic ShieldMF: Glamer (1st level) + Cascade Spell [(alter senses; +1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 min./level; +1 level)] + Cascade Spell (sound lance; +1 level) + Cascade Spell (warding; +1 level) + Shape Spell (emanation; +2 levels) + Reach Spell (close to personal; -1 level) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Extend Spell (inst. to 1 min./level; +3 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Selective Spell (+2 levels) + Reduce Spell (20d6 to 5d6 and auditory only; -3 levels) = 6th level (bard 5th); selectively damages (5d6 sonic/rd.) and dampens sound, or wards off sonic damage, in 10’r. aura.

Cacophonous CallAPG: Sickening touch (0 level) + Reach Spell (touch to close; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to target; +0 levels) + Augment Spell (nausea; +2 levels) + Restricted Spell (bard; -1 level) = 2nd level; target nauseated 1 rd./level (save neg.).

Call Animal CompanionRR2: Figment (0 level) + Augment Spell (visual representation of your location; +1 level) + Phantasmal Spell (-1 level) + Reach Spell (close to line of sight; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to inst.; -1 level) + Creature-Specific Spell (animal companion; -2 levels) = 0 level; calls your animal companion (which receives a mental image of your location) from anywhere within ¼ mile/level.

Call Aquatic Animal IRR: Summon nature’s ally III (3rd level) + Location-Specific Spell (in body of salt water; -2 levels) = 1st level (listed as 2nd); summons 1 crocodile; 1d3 bull sharks, dolphins, ebon eels, octopuses, or squid; or 1d4+1 porpoises.

  • Call aquatic animals II (3rd level; listed as 4th) summons 1 orca or giant octopus; 1d3 giant crocodiles, giant moray eels, tiger sharks, or hammerhead sharks; 1d4+1 blue sharks or crocodiles; or 2d4+1 bull sharks, dolphins, ebon eels, octopuses, or squid.

Call Aquatic Humanoid IRR: Summon monster IV (4th level) + Resistible Spell (Will save applies; -1 level) = 3rd level; summons 1 sea hag or triton, 1d3 sauhuagin, 1d4+1 kuo-toa, or 2d4+1 locathah or merfolk.

Call Aquatic Humanoid IIRR: Summon monster VI (6th level) + Resistible Spell (Will save applies; -1 level) = 5th level (listed as 6th); summons 1 brine hag, 1d4+1 tritons, 2d4+1 sahuagin, 3d6 ku-toa, or 4d8 locathah or merfolk.

Call Aquatic MonsterRR: Summon monster V (5th level) + Resistible Spell (Will save applies; -1 level) = 4th level (listed as 5th); summons 1 elasmosaurus, ichthyosaurus, Large water elemental, marine scrag troll, or 1d3 sea lions or plesiosaurs.

Call ConstructUM: Dimensional skip (1st level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Irresistible Spell (+2 levels) + Reach Spell (close to interplanar; +6 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (construct controlled by you; -2 levels) = 8th level; summons one construct you already control.

Call Dretch HordeBVD: Summon (1st level) + Augment Spell (CR 2 dretch; +2 levels) + Augment Spell (2d4+1 summoned; +1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 hr./level; +3 levels) + Ritual Spell (-2 levels) = 5th level. The numen cost to maintain the effect (5,000 x CL) can be paid by the caster but is more often paid in the form of souls for the dretches to haul back to the Abyss.

Call Forth the BeastHH: Compel (kill everyone you meet; 2nd level) + Cascade Spell (memory lapseAPG; +2 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd. to 1 hr./level; +4 levels) + Delay Spell (when next fall asleep, and after compulsion ends; +1 level) + Creature-Specific Spell (humanoid; -2 levels) + Cascade Spell (damage attribute: Con; -1 level) + Ritual Spell (full round; -1 level) = 5th level; when next falls asleep, target immediately wakes up, goes on a murder spree for 1 hr./level, then forgets what happened. Caster takes 1d4 Con damage.

Call Guardian, LesserAUG: Summon (1st level) + Variable Spell (choose at time of casting; +1 level) + Augment Spell (CR 4; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 hr./level; +3 levels) + Ritual Spell (-2 levels) = 6th level; as summon monster IV (gargoyle, griffon, harpy, minotaur), but ritual casting for much longer service.

Call Guardian, GreaterAUG: Call lesser guardian (q.v.; 6th level) + Augment Spell (CR 7; +2 levels) = 8th level (listed as 9th); dire bear, gorgon, medusa, etc.

Call KolyarutPnH: Summon (1st level) + Accursed Spell (+1 level) + Augment Spell (CR 8 kolyarut; +4 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 hr./level; +3 levels) + Tenacious Spell (+1 level) + Ritual Spell (-2 levels) + Restricted Spell (lawful caster; -1 level) = 7th level; summons one kolyarut inevitable for 1 hr./level. At the end of that time, you can invest 350 x CL numen to keep the kolyarut to complete a specific task taking up to 1 day/level. Call marutPnH is Augmented 2 more steps, for CR 12 (9th level).

Call Lightning: Electric arc (0 level) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to cylinder; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (10’r. to 5’r.; -1 level) + Concentration Spell (standard; +1 level) + Delay Spell (standard action to resume concentration; +1 levels) + Ritual Spell (full round; -1 level) + Restricted Spell (access to Weather domain; -1 level) = 2nd level; damage cap 5d6 (Reflex half) in a 5’r. to a height of 25 ft. You can redirect each round as a standard action. Variants:

  • Call Lightning Storm: Call lightning (q.v., 2nd level) + Reach Spell (medium to long; +1 level) – Widen Spell (+1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 10d6 in 10’r. cylinder up to 50 ft. tall, 1/rd. while you concentrate.
  • Call Lightning, GreaterMW: Call lightning storm (q.v.; 4th level) + Empower Spell (+1 level) + Augment Spell (10d6 to 15d6; +1 level) = 6th level; damage cap 1.5 x 15d6 per bolt.

Call NightmareBVD: Summon (1st level) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) + Augment Spell (CR 8 nightmare; +4 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 min./level; +1 levels) + Ritual Spell (-1 level) + Restricted Spell (access to the Soulcrafting feat; -1 level) = 5th level; invest 10,000 x CL numen to maintain effect (for obvious reasons, this is often paid for in the form of souls).

Call of the EmeraldAUG2: Compel (steal onject; 2nd level) + Accursed Spell (+1 level) + Reach Spell (close to planar; +5 levels) + Expedient Spell (individual HD; -1 level) + Ritual Spell (full round; -1 level) = 6th level; named creature of ≤10 HD must steal the nearest object worth >500 gp it is aware of and doesn’t already own. Invest 1,800 x CL numen to maintain effect past 1 rd.

Call of the SapphireAUG2: As call of the emeraldAUG2 (q.v.), but compulsion is to go home.

Call of the TopazAUG2: As call of the emeraldAUG2 (q.v.), but compulsion is to stand still (as if paralyzed) for 1 round.

Call to MindSRD: Hand of fate (0 level) + Cascade Spell (skill enhancement: Knowledge; +1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) + Interrupting Spell (+1 level) = 1st level; re-roll failed knowledge check with +1/2 levels (+5 max.) bonus.

Call MountBED: Dimensional skip (1st level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Reach Spell (touch to interplanar; +7 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (your bonded mount; -2 levels) + Ritual Spell (full round; -1 level) + Restricted Spell (paladin; -2 levels) = 4th level (listed as 2nd); calls your mount to you, even from across planes.

Call upon FaithTM2: Variable Spell (see below; +1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Sudden Spell (+0 levels) = 1st level; swift action provides one of the following before your next turn:

  • Resistance (0 level) + Augment Spell (+1 to +3; +1 level) = +3 to next saving throw;
  • Skill enhancement (0 level) = +1/2 levels (+5 max.) to next skill check;
  • Attribute boost (0 level) + Augment Spell (+2 to +4; +1 level) = +2 to next attribute check;
  • Blessing (0 level) + Augment Spell (+1 to +3; +1 level) = +3 to attack roll and damage.

Call Upon the PowerAU: Attribute boost (Str; 0 level) + Cascade Spell (attribute boost: Con; +1 level) + Consecrate Spell (+1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 rd./level; -1 level) + Quicken Spell (+3 levels) + Restricted Spell (paladin; -2 levels) = 1st level; swift casting grants +2 sacred bonus to Str and Con for 1 rd./level.
